info.title: Marfa API
info.description:
Marfa stores typed records, called items, and the edges between them. This reference describes its HTTP API.

## Authentication

Send a credential in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer <token>`: an API key (`marfa_k1_…`) or the access token of an app someone signed in to (`marfa_at_…`). In this reference, *you* means the credential that sends the request.

## Recent sign-in

Restoring an archive or a backup, moving the sign-in address, changing `allow_private_addresses` and changing where files and backups go (`backup_path` and the `object_store_` settings other than the access key ID and the secret) also need the owner to have signed in within the last fifteen minutes. An app's access token whose owner signed in longer ago is answered `401 insufficient_user_authentication` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_user_authentication", max_age="900"`, as RFC 9470 describes. Send the owner through `GET /oauth/authorize` with `max_age=900`: Marfa asks them to sign in again, and the tokens the code leads to carry the new sign-in. A refreshed token keeps the time of the sign-in it came from. An API key has no sign-in to renew, so it is refused these acts with `403 app_sign_in_required`, and the private local command makes them without one.

## Local command

An operation marked `x-marfa-local-command` also answers the private local listener: a Unix socket that only the account running the instance can open. The connection is the proof, so the request carries no credential, and no security scheme here describes it. The `marfa` command line reaches it with `--socket`.

## Permissions

Your credential reads and writes only the types its permissions reach. If you ask by ID for an item you can't read, Marfa answers as if the item doesn't exist. An edge appears in a response only if you can read both its edge type and the item it starts from.

## Pagination

A list returns one page at a time, as `{ "data": [...], "next_cursor": "..." }`. To get the next page, send `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. The last page has `next_cursor: null`. A page can be short or empty and still have more after it, so stop only when `next_cursor` is `null`. A list that can't page answers `{ "data": [...] }` alone.

## Answers

An operation that returns one object returns it bare, and wraps it only where the answer holds more than the object. A delete answers `200` with `{ "ok": true }` once the thing is gone, and `200` with the object where the object stays in a new state. No operation answers `204`.

## Query parameters

Every operation refuses a query parameter it doesn't recognize with `400 validation_error`, so a misspelled filter can't silently return everything. A boolean parameter is `true` or `false`, and anything else, `1` and `yes` included, is a `400 validation_error`. The `edge[<type>]` and `backref[<type>]` filters on `GET /items` and `GET /items/stats` are recognized for any type. Marfa ignores any parameter that starts with `_`, so use that prefix for a parameter of your own, such as a cache buster. The OAuth operations `GET /oauth/authorize`, `POST /oauth/token`, `POST /oauth/revoke` and `POST /oauth/device-authorization` ignore a parameter they don't recognize, as RFC 6749 requires.

## Errors

An error answers `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "...", "details": {} } }`. Use `code` in your logic: each operation lists the codes it can return, and the `X-Error-Code` header repeats it. `message` is for people and can change. A version conflict also carries the item or edge as it stands now, in `current`, so you can merge and try again.

The OAuth operations under `/oauth/` answer their own errors in the shape their RFCs define, `{ "error": "...", "error_description": "..." }`, with no `X-Error-Code`. A refusal every operation shares, such as `412` or `429`, keeps the shape above.

## Idempotency

A write that takes an `Idempotency-Key` header is safe to retry. Send the same request with the same key, and Marfa returns the first response, with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, and doesn't write again. A key belongs to the credential that sends it. While the first request with a key is still running, a repeat returns `409 idempotency_key_in_flight` and writes nothing, so retry it. Reusing a key for a different request returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`. Repeating a request after Marfa moves to another contract version returns `422 idempotency_contract_changed`, with the first response's status in `details.original_status`, and doesn't write again.

## Request bodies

A body is JSON, sent with `Content-Type: application/json`. A request that doesn't send its body as JSON returns `400 validation_error` and changes nothing, even if it has no body at all. The exceptions are `POST /blobs`, which takes the bytes of a blob, and `POST /restore`, which takes an archive. `POST /oauth/token`, `POST /oauth/revoke` and `POST /oauth/device-authorization` take a form (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`), as their RFCs define. `POST /oauth/register` takes JSON, and answers a request that isn't JSON with `400 invalid_client_metadata`.

## Time

Every time is UTC, written as `2026-10-03T09:30:00.000Z`. A time field is named for what happened, such as `created_at`. A filter on a time field pairs `_after` and `_before`, and both leave out the time you give, except `updated_after`, which includes it so that nothing changed at the same moment is skipped. `GET /occurrences` takes a window, `from` and `to`, instead.

## Event stream

`GET /events` sends each change as a frame whose `id:` is its event ID, in the order Marfa made the changes. To resume, reconnect with the last ID you received as `Last-Event-ID`, under any `type` or `edges` filter: Marfa replays what you missed, then sends `stream_live`. Marfa reads your credential again before each batch of frames and every 30 seconds: you receive only what it can read now, and a credential that's revoked or expired ends the stream, so reconnect with a current one. Ignore lines that start with `:`.

## Web pages

A web page can connect from a browser with no setup. `POST /oauth/register` and the discovery documents answer any origin, so the page registers itself, then opens the authorization endpoint in a window for the owner to approve. Once the owner approves it, the origin of each redirect URI it registered may call every operation from a browser. Send the access token in `Authorization`: no response allows a browser's credentials.

## Every response

Every response carries `X-Marfa-Contract`, the version of this contract, which is also this document's version. Every response also carries `X-Request-ID`, which identifies the request if you report a problem. Send `X-Marfa-Contract` on every request but a read of `/` and of `/health`, naming the contract version your client was built for. A request that names another version, or a value that is not a whole number, returns `412 contract_mismatch` and changes nothing. A request that names none is served.

ownerSession.name: __Host-marfa_session
ownerSession.description: The owner's browser sign-in, which only the sign-in pages read: here, the passkey doors. On plain HTTP on this machine, the cookie is `marfa_session`. Writes require this instance's Origin, and changes require authentication within fifteen minutes. Apps cannot use this authority.

bearerAuth.description: Authenticate with an API key (`marfa_k1_…`) or an OAuth access token (`marfa_at_…`).

id.description: Unique identifier for the edge type.

label.description: The name an app shows on the from end of an edge of this type, such as `Children` on a parent. Not the `reverse_name`, which is the code name a file writes.

reverse_label.description: The name an app shows on the to end, such as `Parent` on a child. It is the same text as `label` when the relation is two-way, and an app then shows both directions as one list.

description.description: What the edge type is for.

cardinality.description: How many edges of the type an item can hold. `one-to-one`: each item at either end holds one. `one-to-many`: each item at the to end holds one. `many-to-one`: each item at the from end holds one. `many-to-many`: no limit.

from_type_constraints.description: The types the item an edge points from can have: `*`, a type identifier or `role:<name>`. A type matches its subtypes.

to_type_constraints.description: The types the item an edge points to can have, in the same form as `from_type_constraints`.

cascade_on_delete.description: What deleting an edge's end does. `cascade`: deleting the from item trashes the to item. `orphan`: the other stays. `block`: the delete fails. `with-hosts`: the from item is trashed with its last to item, restored with any.

property_schema.description: The properties an edge of the type can carry, by name. Marfa checks an edge's properties against it each time the edge is written, and accepts a property it doesn't list.

reverse_name.description: The name the edge goes by when read from its to end, such as `child-of` for `parent-of`.

written_from.description: The end of an edge whose file writes it in a folder: `from`, or `to` under the reverse name. `none` means no file writes it, so a folder never renders it.

shipped.description: `true` if Marfa ships the edge type: it exists on every instance, and you can't register or delete it. `false` for one registered through `POST /edge-types`.

acyclic.description: `true` if the server refuses an edge of this type that closes a cycle through other edges of the type. Every edge type refuses an edge from an item to itself.

flat.description: `true` if the server refuses an edge of this type from an item whose type its `to_type_constraints` admit, so an item that an edge of the type can point to never points from one.

EdgeType.description: An edge type says how edges of that type behave: its cardinality, what a delete does to the items they join, and which item types they can join.

type.description: The property's type: one of the field types a type's `fields` take, except `thumbnail` and `status`.

description.description: What the property holds.

required.description: `true` if every edge of the type must have the property.

items_type.description: The type of each element of an `array` property. A write is refused if an element is not a value of that type. It can't be `thumbnail`.

format.description: A refinement of a `string` property. `url`, `email` and `date` store it as that type. `bcp47` and `iso3166` only label it, and `currency` limits it to three capital letters. It can't be `thumbnail`.

EdgePropertyDefinition.description: One property an edge of an edge type can carry.

types.description: The types the lever applies to.

TypeLever.description: A lever that applies to the types it names.

types.description: The types the lever applies to.

sources.description: The sources the lever lets through on those types.

TypeAndSourceLever.description: A lever that applies to the types it names, and lets through the sources it names.

types.description: The types the lever applies to.

TypeLeverStrict.description: A lever that applies to the types it names.

types.description: The types the lever applies to.

sources.description: The sources the lever lets through on those types.

TypeAndSourceLeverStrict.description: A lever that applies to the types it names, and lets through the sources it names.

allOf.description: Types on which a write may not set a property the type doesn't declare.
Types that take new items only from the listed sources.

Types whose listings, searches, exports, event streams and webhook deliveries show only items from the listed sources. A read by ID isn't narrowed, and a copy stream sends such items with `listed: false`.

EnforcementOverride.description: A key's own enforcement levers, in the shape `/config` uses. Each lever set here replaces the instance's for this key, looser or stricter; a lever left out stays the instance's.

*.description: Access to every profile field, except that `write` doesn't change the username. Changing the username takes `username` at `write`.

name.description: Access to the owner's name.

username.description: Access to the owner's username, which password sign-in matches. Only this entry at `write` lets a credential change it.

email.description: Access to the owner's email address, which plays no part in signing in.

avatar.description: Access to the owner's profile avatar.

PermissionLevel.description: What a key may do with an entry: `read` it, or `write` it (which includes reading). A name no entry covers is denied.

ItemState.description: An item's lifecycle state. `active`: in use, and what a listing returns by default. `archived`: kept and readable by ID, but left out of a default listing. `trashed`: in the trash until restored or purged. `revoked`: retired for good, on `system.*` items only.

Tier.description: Which layer an item sits in. `library`: what a person chose to keep. `feed`: what arrives in volume from connectors and capture, as it came.

from_id.description: The ID of the item the edge starts from.

to_id.description: The ID of the item the edge points to.

edge_type.description: The identifier of the edge type, such as `parent-of`.

created_at.description: When the edge was created, in UTC.

updated_at.description: When the edge last changed, in UTC.

version.description: The edge's version. It goes up by one on every update, including one that changes nothing.

Edge.description: An edge is a typed, directed relationship from one item to another: `from_id` names the item it points from and `to_id` the item it points to.

kind.description: The recorded sign-in kind. `browser`: the owner's browser. `app`: an app the owner approved. `key`: an API key. `local`: the local command on the server's machine.

id.description: The ID the sign-in has in `GET /owner/sign-ins`, `local` for the local command, or an app's client ID if its sign-in was already gone. It stays the same after the sign-in ends.

name.description: The sign-in's name when the action happened, as `GET /owner/sign-ins` showed it. At most 200 characters.

Writer.description: A sign-in recorded as the one that wrote a version of an item or first installed a plugin, named as it was then.

type.description: The item's type identifier, such as `core.note`.

allOf.description: The item's lifecycle state.
The item's tier. It doesn't apply to `system.*` items, which carry `library`.

version.description: The item's version. It starts at 1 and goes up by one on each update to the item's properties, `tier`, `occurred_at`, `source_id` or type. A change to its state, tags, extensions or edges leaves it as it is.

schema_version.description: The `version` the item's type had when the item was created. Marfa never changes it, even when the item moves to another type, and doesn't act on it.

source.description: The source the item was written under: the writer's own, or one its key claims. It never changes.

source_id.description: The item's identifier at its source. With `source`, it is the item's natural key. Absent if the writer set none.

read_only.description: `true` if every connector with a live write key for the item's type that owns or claims its `source` lists the type in `read_only_types`, so it puts back an edit made in Marfa on its next run. Marfa doesn't refuse the edit.

web_url.description: The item's page at this instance's sign-in address, then `/i/` and the item's ID. Marfa builds it when it answers the item, so it changes when the sign-in address moves.

app_url.description: The item's address for apps on one device: `marfa://`, the instance's ID, then the item's ID. It stays the same when the sign-in address moves.

capture_latitude.description: The latitude where the item was captured. Absent if the writer set none.

capture_longitude.description: The longitude where the item was captured. Absent if the writer set none.

occurred_at.description: When the item happened, in UTC. Defaults to when it was created.

created_at.description: When the item was created, in UTC.

updated_at.description: When the item was last written, in UTC. A tag or extension write moves it too.

last_activity_at.description: When the item or one of its rows last changed, in UTC. A row change moves it and leaves `updated_at` and `version` alone.

trashed_at.description: When the item went to the trash, in UTC, or when a `system.*` item was revoked. A later write to the item leaves it as it is, and a restore clears it. `null` for an item outside the trash, and for one an archive restored to the trash without a time.

trashed_by_cascade.description: Always `true` where present: the item went to the trash with another item, through a cascading edge such as `parent-of`. Present while it stays in the trash. Absent on an item trashed on its own.

trashed_with.description: The ID of the item whose trash took this one into the trash, beside `trashed_by_cascade`, whatever became of that item since. Present only if you can read that item's type.

edges.description: The item's outbound edges you can read, by edge type, each the first page that `GET /items/{id}/edges` continues. Empty if `source_filter` leaves the item out. Absent where an operation doesn't return edges, such as a listing without `include=edges`.

extensions.description: The item's extension namespaces that you can read, each mapped to its data. Present only where `include` names `extensions`.

writer.description: The sign-in that wrote the item's current version, named as it was then, even after it ends. `null` if no sign-in wrote it, such as when Marfa reads a file's text. Present only where `include` names `writer`.

Item.description: An item is one record in Marfa.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last. A page can be short, or empty, with a cursor still to follow, so a walk stops on `null` and never on a short page.

item_id.description: The ID of the item the metadata belongs to.

tags.description: The item's tags.

extensions.description: The item's extension namespaces that you can read, each mapped to its data.

Metadata.description: An item's metadata: its tags and its extension namespaces.

fields.description: The strategy for each field the policy names.

allOf.description: The strategy for a field `fields` doesn't name. Leave it out for `last_writer_wins`.

MergePolicy.description: How Marfa merges conflicting edits to the items of a type: a strategy for each named field, and a default for the rest.

MergeStrategy.description: How Marfa resolves a conflict on one field. `last_writer_wins` takes the later write. `keep_both_copies` keeps the losing value in a new item tagged `conflicted-copy`, with a `derived-from` edge to the original.

code.description: A machine-readable code for the error. Use it in your logic.

message.description: A description of the error for a person to read. It can change, so don't match on it.

VersionConflictError.description: The error block of the `version_conflict` refusal.

code.description: A machine-readable code for the error. Use it in your logic.

message.description: A description of the error for a person to read. It can change, so don't match on it.

AncestorUnavailableError.description: The error block of the `ancestor_unavailable` refusal.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last. A page can be short, or empty, with a cursor still to follow, so a walk stops on `null` and never on a short page.

VersionPage.description: A page of an item's version snapshots, oldest first.

version.description: The item version the snapshot records.

properties.description: The item's properties at this version.

type.description: The type the item had at this version, which an item moved since no longer has. A snapshot is answered only to a credential that may read it.

allOf.description: The item's tier at this version.

occurred_at.description: When the item happened, in UTC, at this version.

source_id.description: The item's `source_id` at this version, or `null` if it had none.

writer.description: The sign-in that wrote this version, named as it was then, even after it ends. Whoever can read the snapshot sees it, such as another app's name or a key's label. `null` if no sign-in wrote it, such as when Marfa reads a file's text.

created_at.description: When Marfa recorded the snapshot, in UTC.

Version.description: A snapshot of an item as it stood at one version, which Marfa records when the item is updated past it.

BulkCounts.description: How many entries of a bulk write had each outcome.

BulkResultOutcome.description: What happened to one entry of a bulk write. `created`: it made a new item or edge. `updated`: it changed an existing one. `skipped`: it wrote nothing, for the reason in `reason`. `errored`: it was refused, and `error` says why.

code.description: A machine-readable code for the error. Use it in your logic.

message.description: A description of the error for a person to read. It can change, so don't match on it.

details.description: More about the error, such as the field it concerns. Each code defines its own details.

BulkEntryError.description: Why one entry of a bulk write is `errored`: the error a single write would return.

version.description: The item version this side shows.

properties.description: The item's properties at this version.

allOf.description: The item's tier at this version.

occurred_at.description: When the item happened, in UTC, at this version.

source_id.description: The item's `source_id` at this version, or `null` if it had none.

type.description: The item's type identifier at this version.

ConflictSnapshot.description: An item as it stood at one version, as a conflict shows it.

title_field.description: The field that holds an item's title for display.

body_field.description: The field that holds an item's body for display. The field holds Markdown, and a `string` field named here holds up to 1,000,000 Unicode characters unless its `max_length` says otherwise.

name_from_body.description: Whether an item with no title is named by the first line of its body. `false` where the body is not a name, such as a highlight's passage: such an item is named after what it comes from, or `Untitled`. Defaults to `true`.

icon.description: The type's icon, as an Iconify ID, `<set>:<name>`, from a pinned version of `lucide` or `simple-icons`, such as `lucide:calendar-days`. On a type read back, the owner's own choice replaces the author's.

DisplayHints.description: How clients show a type and its items: the fields that hold an item's title and body, whether the body names an item, and the type's icon. Each hint comes from the nearest type that sets it.

recent_days.description: How many days back Marfa keeps every version of an item. Counts from now.

daily_snapshot_days.description: How many days back Marfa keeps one version per day, after the recent window. A day is a UTC calendar day.

weekly_snapshot_days.description: How many days back Marfa keeps one version per week, after the daily window. A week is an ISO week. Marfa deletes older versions, but always keeps the latest. 0 deletes no version for its age once it is past the daily window.

max_versions.description: The most versions Marfa keeps for an item. Past it, Marfa drops the oldest first.

VersionPolicy.description: How long Marfa keeps the versions of a type's items. A field you leave out comes from the parent type, then from the instance defaults.

feed_days.description: How many days Marfa keeps a feed item, counted from when it arrived: a whole number from 1 to 36,500. After that Marfa moves the item to the trash. `null` keeps feed items although a parent type expires them. Library items never expire.

RetentionPolicy.description: How long Marfa keeps the feed items of a type. A part you leave out comes from the parent type. A type that no type in its chain gives a window keeps its items.

origin.description: Where the type came from: shipped by Marfa, registered through `POST /types` or a restore, installed by a plugin, or unknown.

name.description: The plugin's name.

version.description: The version of the plugin that last installed the type.

plugin.description: The plugin that installed the type, or `null` for a type no plugin installed. It stays after the plugin is removed.

kind.description: The recorded sign-in kind. `browser`: the owner's browser. `app`: an app the owner approved. `key`: an API key. `local`: the local command on the server's machine.

id.description: The ID the sign-in has in `GET /owner/sign-ins`, `local` for the local command, or an app's client ID if its sign-in was already gone. It stays the same after the sign-in ends.

name.description: The sign-in's name when the action happened, as `GET /owner/sign-ins` showed it. At most 200 characters.

created_by.description: The sign-in that first registered the type, or null when none is recorded.

TypeProvenance.description: Where the type came from, the plugin that installed it, and the sign-in that first registered it when known.

ConnectorProblems.description: The source's current problems, by opaque key. Each message is at most 500 characters. The map has at most 200 entries and 512 KiB serialized as UTF-8. An empty map means no current problems.

BulkActionJobStatus.description: Where a bulk-action job is. `queued`: waiting to run. `in_progress`: running. `completed`: it reached every matched item. `failed`: it stopped early, and `error` says why. `canceled`: it was canceled before it finished.

matched.description: How many items the action matched.

succeeded.description: How many items the action changed. `0` on a dry run.

errored.description: How many matched items the action left unchanged. `0` on a dry run.

dry_run.description: `true` if this was a dry run, which changed nothing.

ids.description: On a dry run, the ID of every matched item. On a job, the IDs of the items it changed, if it changed from 1 to 100 of them; absent otherwise.

errors.description: On a job, the first 100 items it left unchanged, each with its error. Absent otherwise.

blob_hashes_referenced.description: On a purge job, how many distinct blobs the purged items referenced, whether or not anything still references them. Absent otherwise.

settings.description: On a type move, every folder, view and webhook setting that named the old type when the job finished. Absent otherwise.

remaining.description: On a type move, how many items you can see are still of the old type when the job finished, in any state: those it left unchanged and any written since the move began. Absent otherwise.

remaining_hidden.description: On a type move, `true` if items your source filter hides are still of the old type. A move takes only items you can see. Absent otherwise.

settings_rewritten.description: On a type move, `true` if Marfa rewrote `settings` to name the new type. `false` if an item of the old type remains, a setting has a `reason`, or `settings_error` names a refusal; then none was rewritten. Absent otherwise.

settings_error.description: On a type move, why Marfa rewrote none of `settings` once no item of the old type remained: the new type is gone, or a folder or view would refuse its rewrite. Change the setting or register the type, then run the move again. Absent otherwise.

code.description: A machine-readable code for the refusal. Use it in your logic.

message.description: A description of the refusal for a person to read. It can change, so don't match on it.

details.description: More about the refusal, as the setting's own operation gives it.

BulkActionResult.description: What a bulk action did, or for a dry run, what it matched.

code.description: A machine-readable code for the error. Use it in your logic.

message.description: A description of the error for a person to read. It can change, so don't match on it.

details.description: More about the error, such as the field it concerns. Each code defines its own details.

BulkActionError.description: An item a bulk action left unchanged, and why.

kind.description: What holds the setting.

id.description: The ID of the folder, view or webhook. Absent when you can't read it.

field.description: The setting that names the type: `query.types`, `query.filter`, `defaults.type`, `first_placement` or `type_filter`.

reason.description: Why a move can't rewrite the setting: `not_permitted`, you can't change it; `filter_term`, its filter can't be rewritten safely; `placement_conflict`, it places the types apart; `subtypes`, a webhook can't name both.

message.description: What to change before moving, for a person to read. Present with `reason`.

TypeSetting.description: A folder, view or webhook setting that names a type.

ViewField.description: A field: an own field (`title`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `occurred_at`, `last_activity_at`, `type`, `state`, `tier`, `tags`) or `properties.<name>`.

allOf.description: The field to sort by.

ViewSort.description: One key a view sorts by.

by.description: The field to group by: an own field (`title`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `occurred_at`, `type`, `state`, `tier` or `tags`), `properties.<name>`, `source`, `status_group`, `edge[<type>]` or `backref[<type>]` for the item an edge of that type joins.

bucket.description: For a date field, the span each group covers. For `tags`, a property or an edge type, `presence` groups by whether the item has a value, with the keys `false` and `true`. Absent groups by the value.

items.description: A value of the field the view groups by.

order.description: The values whose groups come first, in this order. Other groups follow. With `status_group`, the four status group names or `null`. With `presence`, `true` or `false`.

items.description: A value of the field the view groups by.

hidden.description: The values whose groups the view leaves out. With `status_group`, the four status group names or `null`. With `presence`, `true` or `false`.

ViewGroup.description: How a view groups its items.

name.description: The instance's display name. Defaults to `Marfa`.

version.description: The release the instance runs, such as `0.0.14`.

instance_id.description: Unique identifier for the instance. `GET /config` and an archive's manifest show the same value.

contract.description: The contract version, the same number as this document's `info.version`. It stays at `0` until the first public release.

features.description: The features the instance serves, such as `items` and `webhooks`.

max_request_bytes.description: The largest body, in bytes, the instance takes in an ordinary JSON request. A larger one is answered `413 request_too_large`. Bulk writes, blob uploads and a few other operations have their own limits.

InstanceDescription.description: An instance: its identity, build, contract version, features and request size.

code.description: A machine-readable code for the error. Use it in your logic.

message.description: A description of the error for a person to read. It can change, so don't match on it.

components.description: Each component checked: reading and writing the database, free disk space and the blob store.

location.description: The location the server runs in.

country.description: The country the server runs in.

placement.description: Where the server runs. Present only when it is configured.

version.description: The build the instance runs, when it is known.

status.description: `ok`: on schedule, with the last backup whole. `incomplete`: files it names have no recorded copy. `failing`: a run failed or lost files, a store refuses copies, or a part is damaged, so overall `status` is at least `degraded`. `off`: none scheduled.

reason.description: Why backups are `off` or `failing`: `no_backup_destination` when no destination is set, `destination_unusable` when the one set can't be used, or `turned_off` when `backup_interval_seconds` is 0. `destination_unusable` wins if both apply.

destination.description: Where Marfa puts backups: `folder` for the backup folder `backup_path` names, `bucket` for the object store `object_store_bucket` names. Present only for a caller that holds `instance.read`, and only when the settings name one.

last_backup.description: The name of the last backup Marfa put. Present only for a caller that holds `instance.read`.

last_backup_at.description: When Marfa took the last backup it put. Present only for a caller that holds `instance.read`.

failures.description: How many backup runs in a row have failed or lost files. Present only for a caller that holds `instance.read`.

last_error.description: What went wrong in the last failed run, or which files the last backup was put without. Present only for a caller that holds `instance.read`.

last_failed_at.description: When the last failed run ended. Present only for a caller that holds `instance.read`.

copies_waiting.description: How many files waited for their copy in the object store or backup folder when `blob-replicate` last ran. Present only for a caller that holds `instance.read`, and only when a destination is set.

last_backup_files_waiting.description: How many files the last backup names with no recorded copy in the destination, or `null` when unknown. `blob-integrity` keeps the record true. Present only for a caller that holds `instance.read`, and only when a destination is set.

store_error.description: Why the object store or backup folder isn't taking copies, or `null` while it does. It covers a backup folder whose disk isn't there and a destination that can't be used. Present only for a caller that holds `instance.read`.

damaged_parts.description: How many parts a check found altered or, in a backup folder, unreadable, and not since stored again or found whole, or `null` when unknown. Present only for a caller that holds `instance.read`, and only when a destination is set.

backups.description: Whether Marfa backs itself up to its backup folder or object store, how the last backup went, and whether the place it backs up to is taking copies.

name.description: The job's name.

at.description: When the failed run finished, in UTC.

items.description: A housekeeping job whose last run failed.

failed.description: Every job here whose last run failed, or `null` if the schedule can't be read in time.

unreadable_settings.description: The keys of stored settings that no longer read, which Marfa runs on their defaults.

reason.description: Why the jobs that delete are held. `clock_ahead`: the server's clock is more than 7 days later than the trusted time.

clock_at.description: What the server's clock reads, in UTC.

trusted_at.description: The trusted time, in UTC: the time last confirmed or, if later, the latest time the server's clock read since while clean-up was not held.

ends_at.description: When the hold ends if the clock runs without jumping until then, in UTC. `marfa housekeeping confirm-clock` on the server ends it at once.

held.description: Why the jobs that delete old records do nothing, or `null` if they run.

housekeeping.description: What needs attention in the background work. Present only for a caller that holds `instance.read`.

Health.description: The instance's health: the worst state of its components, and each one's state.

retention_days.description: How many days after deletion an item becomes eligible for automatic expiry; zero disables expiry.

TrashPage.description: A page of trashed item summaries.

eligible_for_deletion_at.description: When automatic deletion becomes eligible under the effective policy, or null when disabled or the date is unknown. The sweep may delete it later.

trashed_at.description: When the item entered the trash, or null if not recorded.

kind.description: The recorded sign-in kind. `browser`: the owner's browser. `app`: an app the owner approved. `key`: an API key. `local`: the local command on the server's machine.

id.description: The ID the sign-in has in `GET /owner/sign-ins`, `local` for the local command, or an app's client ID if its sign-in was already gone. It stays the same after the sign-in ends.

name.description: The sign-in's name when the action happened, as `GET /owner/sign-ins` showed it. At most 200 characters.

trashed_by.description: The sign-in that moved the item to the trash, captured at that time, or null if not recorded.

TrashSummary.description: A trashed item’s summary and recorded deletion identity.

type.description: The item type identifier.

version.description: The version to pass when changing this item.

name.description: The item's plain-text name, derived from its type's display hints and fallback fields.

source.description: The source that added the item.

created_at.description: When the item was created, in UTC.

web_url.description: The item's page at this instance's sign-in address, then `/i/` and the item's ID. Marfa builds it when it answers the item, so it changes when the sign-in address moves.

app_url.description: The item's address for apps on one device: `marfa://`, the instance's ID, then the item's ID. It stays the same when the sign-in address moves.

ItemSummary.description: An item's name, source and creation time, without its content.

data.description: The trashed items on this page.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last. A page can be short, or empty, with a cursor still to follow, so a walk stops on `null` and never on a short page.

enrichment_ocr_enabled.description: `true` if file reading includes image text. Enabling reconsiders previously skipped images. Absent: the environment default applies.

error_reporting_enabled.description: `true` if exception reports are sent. Enabling requires both `posthog_host` and `posthog_project_token`. Absent: the environment default applies.

telemetry_enabled.description: `true` if Marfa sends telemetry about itself: traces, log records and metrics to the OTLP endpoints, and exception reports to `posthog_host`. `false` sends none of them and keeps every telemetry setting. Absent: `true`.

otel_sample_ratio.description: The share of traces Marfa exports, from 0 to 1. A trace that holds an error is exported whatever this says. Absent: `0.05`.

otel_service_name.description: The service name on everything Marfa exports, in place of a `service.name` in `otel_resource_attributes`. Absent: `marfa-server`. An archive doesn't carry it.

otel_resource_attributes.description: Attributes Marfa adds to everything it exports, as comma-separated `key=value` pairs with percent-encoded values. One named here replaces Marfa's own of the same name, such as `service.version`. An archive doesn't carry it.

heartbeat_enabled.description: `true` if scheduled heartbeat requests are sent. Enabling requires `heartbeat_url`. Absent: the environment default applies.

name.description: The instance's display name, without control or bidirectional formatting characters. Spaces at each end are trimmed. Absent: `Marfa`.

Types whose listings, searches, exports, event streams and webhook deliveries show only items from the listed sources. A read by ID isn't narrowed, and a copy stream sends such items with `listed: false`.

enforcement.description: The instance's enforcement levers. Each applies to every credential that doesn't set the same lever itself. Absent: no lever is on.

audit_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps audit log entries and outbound webhook delivery history. `0` keeps them with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

event_log_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps events, which a stream can replay from a cursor, and the answers it replays for an `Idempotency-Key`. `0` keeps them with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

trash_retention_days.description: Days an item stays in the trash before Marfa purges it. `0` keeps them with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

row_log_retention_days.description: Days a table keeps a batch in its change log, so you can undo it. `0` keeps them with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

inbound_handled_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps inbound webhook deliveries a connector has marked handled. `0` keeps them with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

inbound_pending_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps inbound webhook deliveries no connector has marked handled. `0` keeps them with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

backup_path.description: The absolute path of the folder Marfa backs itself up to and keeps a second copy of each file in, outside the data directory and the blob folder. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: no backup folder.

object_store_bucket.description: The bucket of an S3-compatible object store that also keeps each file and the backups: 1 to 255 ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `:`, `-` and `_`, other than `.` and `..`. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: no object store.

object_store_region.description: The region of the object store: a name of 1 to 63 ASCII letters, digits, hyphens and underscores that can be part of a host name, such as `us-east-1` or `auto`. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: `us-east-1`.

object_store_endpoint.description: The endpoint of the object store, an `http` or `https` URL with no user name or password. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: the store's provider chooses it.

object_store_path_style.description: `true` if the store at `object_store_endpoint` is addressed by path. `false` puts the bucket, as lowercase host labels, before the endpoint's host, a name without the bucket. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: `true`.

object_store_prefix.description: The folder in the bucket Marfa keeps files and backups under, as `/`-joined segments. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: `marfa`.

object_store_access_key_id.description: The access key ID for the object store.

allow_private_addresses.description: `true` if Marfa may send webhooks, the heartbeat, exception reports and object store requests to loopback, private and other addresses that aren't public. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: `false`.

secrets_set.description: The key of each secret setting stored with a value Marfa can read, present only while one is. Marfa never returns a secret's value.

allOf.description: What the move did and what the owner does next. Present only in the answer to the write that moved the sign-in address.

max_request_bytes.description: The largest request body Marfa accepts, in bytes. Marfa waits 180 seconds for a body, so a body over about 21 MiB can't arrive in time over a 1 Mbit/s link.

max_bulk_request_bytes.description: The largest body the bulk operations accept, in bytes, and the largest row a restore reads. The most you can set is 33554432, half the 67108864 bytes a restore reads on one archive line.

disk_reserve_bytes.description: Free disk space an upload must leave on the blob volume, in bytes. `0` refuses no write for room, and health still reports the disk as degraded below 64 MiB.

blob_min_copies.description: The fewest live copies Marfa keeps of each blob.

blob_cleanup_enabled.description: `true` if the `blob-orphans` job purges blobs nothing references once they have stood in the orphan report for `blob_cleanup_grace_seconds`.

blob_cleanup_grace_seconds.description: How long a blob nothing references stands in the orphan report before a later run purges it, in seconds.

backup_interval_seconds.description: How often Marfa makes a backup when anything it holds has changed, in seconds. `0` turns scheduled backups off.

rate_limit_enabled.description: `true` if the rate limiter is on for requests a key or app makes, app registrations, device code requests, passkey sign-in challenges and deliveries to inbound addresses.

rate_limit_requests.description: How many requests one key or app may make in each rate-limit window, across every operation.

rate_limit_keys_requests.description: How many requests one key may make in each rate-limit window to the operations under `/keys`.

rate_limit_window_seconds.description: How long one rate-limit window lasts, in seconds.

unapproved_app_retention_hours.description: Hours Marfa keeps an app that registered itself and holds no grant. `0` keeps it with no age limit.

revoked_grant_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps a revoked app grant. `0` keeps it with no age limit.

enrichment_max_blob_bytes.description: The largest file Marfa reads whole to extract its text, in bytes. Marfa skips a larger file unread, and reads a sound or video from its headers whatever its size.

enrichment_max_text_chars.description: The most Unicode characters of extracted text Marfa keeps, counted as characters and not UTF-16 code units. Marfa cuts longer text short.

enrichment_max_inflated_bytes.description: The most a document may inflate to when Marfa extracts its text, all its parts together, in bytes. Marfa skips a document that inflates past it.

enrichment_max_memory_bytes.description: The most memory the process that reads one file may take, in bytes. Marfa skips a file that needs more.

enrichment_max_attempts.description: How many times Marfa tries to read a file that fails, or that stops the server, before it stops trying.

update_check_enabled.description: `true` if Marfa checks GitHub for new releases every few hours. When `false`, it makes no request for them and reports no release as newer.

event_stream_max_viewers.description: The most event-stream viewers one server serves at once. `0` sets no limit.

mcp_fetch_enabled.description: `true` if MCP tools fetch a file from a web address, or a file a chat attached, to save it. When `false`, a tool asked to fetch one is refused.

mcp_fetch_max_bytes.description: The largest file an MCP tool fetches from a web address to save, in bytes. Marfa refuses a larger file and stores nothing.

mcp_fetch_timeout_seconds.description: How long an MCP tool's fetch of a file from a web address may take, from connecting to the last byte, in seconds.

inbound_max_bytes.description: The largest inbound webhook delivery Marfa stores, in bytes.

rate_limit_inbound_requests.description: How many requests one inbound endpoint's address takes in each rate-limit window, whatever each is answered.

inbound_in_flight_bytes.description: The most bytes of inbound webhook deliveries Marfa holds in memory at once. One source holds at most half.

inbound_backlog_deliveries.description: The unhandled deliveries one registration may hold before Marfa refuses more for it.

inbound_backlog_bytes.description: The bytes of unhandled deliveries one registration may hold before Marfa refuses more for it.

webhook_backlog_deliveries.description: Maximum number of pending deliveries per webhook. Marfa records a new delivery as `canceled` if adding it would exceed this limit.

webhook_backlog_bytes.description: Maximum total payload size in bytes for a webhook's pending deliveries. Marfa records a new delivery as `canceled` if adding its payload would exceed this total.

inbound_retained_deliveries.description: The most deliveries one registration retains across its live and retired endpoints.

inbound_retained_bytes.description: The most bytes of bodies, headers and queries one registration retains across its live and retired endpoints.

cors_origins.description: The browser origins allowed to call the API across origins with a token, beside the web pages the owner approves. Each is an origin with no path.

InstanceConfig.description: The instance configuration: its display name, enforcement levers and live settings, with the instance's ID.

created_at.description: When the sign-in was made, in UTC. For an app, when the owner last approved it.

last_used_at.description: When a recorded use occurred, in UTC, or `null` if none is recorded. Uses are recorded at most once a minute for browsers and once an hour for apps or keys. Failed recording leaves the previous value.

expires_at.description: When the sign-in ends unless used again, in UTC. For an app, the inactivity boundary. `null` for disabled app inactivity retirement or a key without an expiry.

client_ip.description: The IP address a browser signed in from, or `null` for an app, a key, or a browser whose address Marfa could not tell.

user_agent.description: The `User-Agent` a browser sent when it signed in, or `null` for an app, a key, or a browser that sent none.

minted_by.description: For a key an app minted, the ID of that app's sign-in while the app is signed in. `null` for a browser, an app, an owner's key (`owner_key`), any other key, and a key whose app has ended.

id.description: Unique identifier for the app's grant.

kind.description: `cli` registered with the `marfa` command line's `software_id`; otherwise `web` has approved web origins, and `app` is any other app.

client_id.description: The ID of the registered app.

client_name.description: The app's registered name, or null if unavailable.

origins.description: Approved web origins, empty for a native app.

scopes.description: The access the owner approved for the app.

vendors.description: Each `app.<vendor>` namespace the app holds. `GET /app-vendors/{vendor}/data` lists what it keeps there.

granted_at.description: When the owner last approved the app, in UTC.

last_used_at.description: When the app last used its access, in UTC, or null if never used.

AppGrant.description: An app's standing access to Marfa.

revoked_keys.description: How many keys the app made, or those keys made, Marfa revoked because they reached beyond the resulting scope set.

redirect_uris.description: The addresses Marfa may send a person back to after authorization. Required for `authorization_code`. At most 10. A `web` client's URIs must use `https` off the loopback; a `native` client may use `http` on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`.

scope.description: Space-separated scopes to register the client for. `offline_access` needs `refresh_token` or `authorization_code` in `grant_types`. Leave it out for your content and links: `content:read content:write edge.*:read edge.*:write offline_access`.

client_name.description: The app's name, which Marfa shows a person asked to approve it.

client_uri.description: The app's home page URL. Leave it out if the app has none.

logo_uri.description: The app's logo URL. Leave it out if the app has none.

contacts.description: Contact addresses for the app. Leave it out if there are none.

tos_uri.description: The app's terms of service URL. Leave it out if the app has none.

policy_uri.description: The app's privacy policy URL. Leave it out if the app has none.

software_id.description: The software's identifier. Leave it out if there is none.

software_version.description: The software's version. Leave it out if there is none.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description: `none`: the client is public and proves itself with PKCE. Any other method is refused with `invalid_client_metadata`.

grant_types.description: The grants the client uses: `authorization_code`, `refresh_token` or `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`. Defaults to `authorization_code`. Without `authorization_code`, add `refresh_token` to get a refresh token with `offline_access`.

response_types.description: The response types the client uses. Defaults to `code` when `grant_types` includes `authorization_code`.

application_type.description: `web` or `native`, which decides the redirect URIs the client may use. Defaults to `web`.

resources.description: Resource identifiers, each an absolute URI without a fragment; any other value is refused with `invalid_target`. Marfa doesn't register them or return them: a token request names its own `resource`.

OAuthClientRegistration.description: An OAuth client: its app metadata and the grants it uses. Marfa ignores metadata it doesn't support and leaves it out of the answer.

url.description: The URL Marfa posts events to.

events.description: The events Marfa sends, such as `item.created`.

type_filter.description: The type, with its subtypes, or the pattern whose item events Marfa sends. `null` when Marfa sends item events of every type. Edge events aren't filtered.

secret.description: The key Marfa signs each delivery with. Only `POST /webhooks` returns it whole; other responses show `****` and its last four characters.

active.description: `true` if Marfa sends events to the webhook.

created_at.description: When the webhook was created, in UTC.

updated_at.description: When the webhook last changed, in UTC.

Webhook.description: A webhook sends the events you choose, as you can read them, to a URL.

next_cursor.description: Always `null`: Marfa returns every webhook you can inspect in one page.

WebhookPage.description: A page holding every webhook you can inspect.

kind.description: Whether a key or an app registered the webhook.

id.description: The key ID or OAuth client ID.

name.description: The maker's current name, or null if it is no longer available.

maker.description: The credential that registered this webhook.

WebhookRead.description: A webhook sends the events you choose, as you can read them, to a URL.

details.description: More about the error, such as the field it concerns. Each code defines its own details.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last. A page can be short, or empty, with a cursor still to follow, so a walk stops on `null` and never on a short page.

WebhookDeliveryPage.description: A page of a webhook's deliveries, newest first.

id.description: Unique identifier for the delivery. Marfa sends it as `delivery_id`, the same on every attempt.

status.description: `pending`: waiting to be sent or retried. `succeeded`: the receiver answered with a `2xx` status. `failed`: Marfa gave up, and you can redeliver it. `canceled`: Marfa settled it unsent, and `error` says why.

webhook_id.description: The ID of the webhook the delivery belongs to.

status_code.description: The HTTP status the receiver answered on the latest recorded attempt, or `null` if that attempt got no answer or no attempt has run.

attempt.description: How many attempts have recorded an outcome, across every redelivery. A send whose outcome was lost, such as during a restart, isn't counted, so the receiver may have seen more.

error.description: Why the latest attempt failed, or why Marfa settled the delivery unsent. `null` after a success or before the first attempt.

created_at.description: When Marfa queued the delivery, in UTC.

WebhookDelivery.description: A delivery is one event Marfa sends, or tries to send, to a webhook's URL.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last. A page can be short, or empty, with a cursor still to follow, so a walk stops on `null` and never on a short page.

AuditEntryPage.description: One page of audit log entries.

kind.description: The recorded sign-in kind. `browser`: the owner's browser. `app`: an app the owner approved. `key`: an API key. `local`: the local command on the server's machine.

id.description: The ID the sign-in has in `GET /owner/sign-ins`, `local` for the local command, or an app's client ID if its sign-in was already gone. It stays the same after the sign-in ends.

name.description: The sign-in's name when the action happened, as `GET /owner/sign-ins` showed it. At most 200 characters.

kind.description: Marfa acting without a sign-in.

name.description: The server actor name.

actor.description: The sign-in name and kind recorded when the action happened, Marfa for server work, or null when unknown.

created_at.description: When Marfa recorded the entry, in UTC.

key_id.description: The ID of the credential that acted, or `null` if the entry names none, as for Marfa's own housekeeping.

resource_type.description: The kind of resource acted on, such as `key`.

resource_id.description: The ID of the resource acted on, or `null` if there is none.

client_ip.description: The IP address of the request that acted, or `null` if the entry records none.

details.description: More about the action. What it holds depends on `action`.

AuditEntry.description: An audit log entry records one action and who took it.

MetricCount.description: Number of keys that haven't been revoked or expired.

ItemEventFrame.description: An item event: a change to an item, or, as `metadata.changed`, to its tags or extensions. Except on a copy stream, you receive it only if your source filter shows the item.

event_type.description: The event, which is also the frame's `event:`.

allOf.description: The item after the change. On `item.trashed` and `item.purged` of an item a cascade trashed, it carries `trashed_by_cascade`, and `trashed_with` if you can read that item's type.

metadata.description: The item's tags and extensions after the change, or before it on `item.purged`, with only the namespaces you can read. A webhook sends `null`.

restored_with.description: On `item.restored` of an item another item's restore brought back: the ID of that item, if you can read its type.

listed.description: Only on a copy stream: `true` if the item is in the set you can list, `false` if you can read it only by ID.

EdgeEventFrame.description: An edge event: a change to an edge. You receive it only if you can read both the edge type and `from_type`, and, except on a copy stream, only if your source filter shows the item the edge points from.

event_type.description: The event, which is also the frame's `event:`.

allOf.description: The edge after the change, or before it for `edge.deleted`.

from_type.description: The type of the item the edge points from when the event happened.

purged_with.description: On `edge.deleted` of an edge a purge removed: the ID of the purged item.

StreamCursorFrame.description: The stream's first frame, with no `id:`: where the log stood when the stream opened. If Marfa can't read the log within 5 seconds, an ordinary stream leaves it out, so don't wait for it, and a copy stream ends with `stream_incomplete`.

event_type.description: The frame's name, which is also its `event:`.

cursor.description: The ID of the latest event in the log, or `0` if it's empty. Read state after this frame, and you can resume from this ID without missing a change.

instance_id.description: Only on a copy stream: the instance's ID, as `GET /` returns it.

reach.description: Only on a copy stream: the reach to send as `X-Marfa-Reach`, to resume or to read the working copy's data.

StreamLiveFrame.description: Sent once, with no `id:`, when the catch-up is over: everything up to `cursor` has been sent or withheld, and what follows is live. A stream that ends early never sends it.

event_type.description: The frame's name, which is also its `event:`.

cursor.description: A position you can resume from without receiving again what the catch-up covered. `null` only on a copy stream, when Marfa couldn't read the log in time and had nothing to replay.

instance_id.description: Only on a copy stream: the instance's ID, as `GET /` returns it.

reach.description: Only on a copy stream: the reach to send as `X-Marfa-Reach`, to resume or to read the working copy's data.

StreamIncompleteFrame.description: The last frame, with no `id:`, when the stream can no longer deliver what it opened with. Marfa sends nothing past the gap, so reconnect with the last `id:` you received. Marfa closes a stream whose reader takes nothing for 30 seconds, with no frame.

event_type.description: The frame's name, which is also its `event:`.

reason.description: `credential_ended`: your credential ended. `read_failed`: Marfa couldn't read the log or your credential. `server_stopping`: Marfa is stopping.

cursor.description: The ID of the last event the stream sent, or `null` if it sent none.

CatchupTooOldFrame.description: The last frame, with no `id:`, when the log no longer holds the events after your `Last-Event-ID`, or the stream reaches an event Marfa can't read. Read state again from the API, then open a new stream.

event_type.description: The frame's name, which is also its `event:`.

min_retained_id.description: The ID of the oldest event the log still holds.

requested.description: The `Last-Event-ID` you sent, or the ID of the latest event when you sent none.

CursorAheadFrame.description: The last frame, with no `id:`, when your `Last-Event-ID` is past the latest event in the log, as after the instance is restored to an earlier state. Read state again from the API.

event_type.description: The frame's name, which is also its `event:`.

head.description: The ID of the latest event in the log.

ReachChangedFrame.description: The last frame of a copy stream, with no `id:`, when its reach changes, such as after a retype or a narrowed key. Rebuild the working copy.

event_type.description: The frame's name, which is also its `event:`.

EventStreamFrame.description: One frame of `GET /events`. Its `event_type` is also its `event:`.

WebhookItemEvent.description: The body of a webhook delivery of an item event.

event_id.description: The event's ID in the log, the same as its `id:` on `GET /events`.

delivery_id.description: The ID of the delivery, the same on every attempt. Use it to recognize a repeat.

delivered_at.description: When Marfa sent this attempt, in UTC.

WebhookEdgeEvent.description: The body of a webhook delivery of an edge event.

WebhookEvent.description: The body of a webhook delivery: the event, with its ID and the delivery's.

Backup.description: A backup in the instance's backup folder or object store.

code.description: A machine-readable code for the error. Use it in your logic.

message.description: A description of the error for a person to read. It can change, so don't match on it.

details.description: More about the error, such as the field it concerns. Each code defines its own details.

code.description: What happens: `browser_sessions_end`, `passkeys_unusable` or `apps_sign_in_again` when the sign-in address moves, `address_removed` for each address that is dropped.

sentence.description: The consequence, in a sentence for a person to read.

count.description: How many sessions, passkeys or apps it affects, or `null` for an address that is dropped.

AddressConsequence.description: One thing a change of address does.

sign_in_address.description: The sign-in address after the change.

requires_confirmation.description: `true` if a write of this change needs `confirm_sign_in_address_change: true`: the sign-in address of a claimed instance moves.

consequences.description: Everything the change does, empty if it does nothing.

next_steps.description: What the owner would do after the change, in order. Empty unless the sign-in address moves.

passed.description: `true` if the new sign-in address answered `GET /` as this instance, `false` if it didn't, and `null` if Marfa didn't ask it.

reason.description: Why it didn't pass: `unreachable`, nothing answered; `timed_out`, no answer in 5 seconds; `not_this_instance`, something else answered; `needs_recent_sign_in`, the address isn't public and you couldn't make the move. Present if `passed` isn't `true`.

sign_in_address_check.description: Whether the new sign-in address answers as this instance, as a write of the change checks it. Present when `requires_confirmation` is `true`.

AddressCheck.description: What a change of address would do. Nothing is written.

sign_in_address.description: The sign-in address to try, an origin with no path. `null` tries removing it, so the server's default applies.

addresses.description: The addresses to try, each an origin with no path. `null` tries removing them, so the server's default applies.

AddressCheckRequest.description: The address change to check, written as `PATCH /config` writes it.

key.description: The setting's key, the field `/config` reads and writes.

description.description: What the setting does.

value.description: The value in force now: the stored one if it reads, else the default.

default.description: The value the setting takes when nothing is stored.

stored.description: The value stored for it, `null` if none is, or the stored text itself if it no longer reads.

rule.description: The values the setting accepts, in words.

unreadable.description: `true` if the stored value no longer reads. Marfa then uses the default. Present only then.

together.description: The keys of the other settings a rule across settings ties to this one.

secret.description: `true` if the setting holds a secret. Marfa then answers `value`, `default` and `stored` as `null`.

set.description: `true` if a secret setting holds a value Marfa can read. Present only for a secret.

ConfigSetting.description: A stored setting: its value, its default and the rule it follows.

name.description: The rule's name.

description.description: What the rule requires of the settings it names.

keys.description: The keys of the settings the rule holds together.

ConfigSettingRule.description: A rule that holds across several settings.

name.description: The environment variable that sets it.

description.description: What the setting does.

secret.description: `true` if the setting holds a secret, which Marfa never shows.

StartOnlySetting.description: A setting only the environment sets, read when Marfa starts.

rules.description: Every rule that holds across settings.

start_only.description: Every setting only the environment sets.

ConfigSettings.description: Every setting Marfa has: the stored ones, the rules across them and the ones only the environment sets.

type.description: The column's type. `item` holds the ID of an item, and `type_constraints` may name the types it accepts. The others are as a field of that type.

label.description: A name for people to read, up to 100 characters. Leave it out and a type read answers one made from the column's name, such as `Due At` for `due_at`. The type list answers only the declared label.

description.description: What the column holds.

required.description: `true` if every row must have a value for the column.

format.description: A refinement of a `string` column, as a field's `format`. Not for an `item` column.

max_length.description: The longest value a `string` or `enum` column allows. Not for an `item` column.

minimum.description: The lowest value the column allows, itself included. Only a `number` or `integer` column takes it.

maximum.description: The highest value the column allows, itself included. Only a `number` or `integer` column takes it.

type_constraints.description: The identifiers of the types an `item` column accepts. Each must be registered, or be the type that declares the column. Leave it out to accept any type.

adds_up.description: How the column totals: `sum` and `average` for a `number` or `integer` column, `min` and `max` also for a `date` or `datetime` column, and `count` of the rows that hold a value for any column. Leave it out for no total.

searchable.description: `true` to feed full-text search from a `string`, `email` or `url` column. Defaults to `false`, unlike a field.

ColumnDefinition.description: One column of a table: its type, and how rows may fill it.

label.description: A name for people to read, up to 100 characters. Leave it out and a type read answers one made from the table's name, such as `Line Items` for `line_items`.

description.description: What the table holds.

columns.description: The table's columns, by name: at least one and at most 64.

order.description: The name of a `datetime`, `number`, `integer` or `string` column whose order the server keeps for the rows, so a page sorted by it reads only the rows it answers. Changing or removing it needs `schema.write`.

TableDefinition.description: One table a type declares: the rows an item of the type holds under a name, in the columns it lists.

TableRow.description: A row of an item's table. A row is never an item: it has no version, tags or edges.

id.description: Unique identifier for the row, a UUIDv7.

values.description: The row's values, keyed by column. A column with no value is left out.

updated_at.description: When the row last changed, in UTC.

withheld.description: Present when a column of type `item` names an item you can't read: those columns, left out of `values`.

TableRowPage.description: A page of a table's rows.

next_cursor.description: Pass this as `cursor` to get the next page, or `null` when there are no more.

TableSummary.description: A table an item's type declares, with what the item holds in it.

name.description: The table's name.

label.description: The table's label, or one made from its name.

row_count.description: How many rows the item holds in the table.

bytes.description: The size of the rows' values as JSON, in bytes.

last_batch.description: The ID of the last batch that changed a row of the table, or `null` if none has.

changed_at.description: When a row of the table last changed, in UTC, or `null` if none has.

TableSummaryPage.description: The tables an item's type declares, by name.

next_cursor.description: Always `null`: Marfa returns every table in one page.

RowOperation.description: One change to a row: `put` creates or replaces a whole row, `patch` sets the columns it names, and `delete` removes a row.

op.description: `put` writes the whole row, `patch` sets only the columns in `values`, and `delete` removes the row.

id.description: The ID of the row, a UUIDv7 in lowercase. Required for `patch` and `delete`. Leave it out of a `put` for Marfa to create one.

values.description: The values, keyed by column. The row an operation leaves holds at most 65536 bytes (64 KiB) of values as JSON. On a `patch`, `null` clears a column. A `put` keeps each value that names an item you can't read. A `delete` takes none.

RowBatchResult.description: What a batch of row changes did.

batch.description: The ID of the batch, or `null` when it changed no row.

last_activity_at.description: The time of the batch, in UTC, which each row it changed took as its `updated_at`, or the item's own `last_activity_at` when the batch changed no row. An item that held a later `last_activity_at` keeps it.

results.description: One entry per operation, in the order you sent them.

items.description: What one operation did to its row.

outcome.description: `created`, `replaced`, `patched` or `deleted` for a change, `unchanged` when the row already held the values, `absent` for a delete of a row that wasn't there.

RowTotals.description: The totals of a table's columns that add up, over the rows a filter selects.

row_count.description: How many rows the filter selects.

totals.description: For each column that names `adds_up`, an object with that way as its one key: `sum` and `count` are `0` over no values, and `average`, `min` and `max` are `null`.

RowsChangedFrame.description: One batch of changes to an item's table. You receive it if you can read the item's type and your source filter shows the item. Copy streams never receive it.

event_type.description: The event, which is also the frame's `event:`.

type.description: The item's type.

source.description: The item's source.

undoes.description: Present when the batch is an undo: the ID of the batch it undid.

last_activity_at.description: The time of the batch, in UTC. An item that held a later `last_activity_at` keeps it.

values_included.description: Present, as `false`, when the batch's values were too large to carry: each entry of `rows` then holds only its `id`, and `deleted` for a removed row.

rows.description: Each row the batch changed, as the batch left it, or with `deleted` `true` for a removed row. A row changed at `last_activity_at`.

values.description: The row's values after the batch.

deleted.description: Present, as `true`, when the batch removed the row.

withheld.description: Present when a column of type `item` names an item you can't read: those columns, left out of `values`.

WebhookRowsEvent.description: The body of a webhook delivery of a rows event.

RowBatchEntry.description: A batch a table's change log holds.

at.description: When the batch was made, in UTC.

rows.description: How many rows the batch changed.

undoes.description: The ID of the batch this one undid, or `null` when it's not an undo.

RowBatchPage.description: The batches a table's change log holds, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Pass this as `cursor` to get the next page. `null` when there are no more.

batch.description: The ID of the undo's own batch, or `null` when every row already stood as it was before the undone batch. Undo this batch to redo the one it undid.

undoes.description: The ID of the batch you undid.

last_activity_at.description: The time of the undo, in UTC, which each row it changed took as its `updated_at`, or the item's own `last_activity_at` when the undo changed no row. An item that held a later `last_activity_at` keeps it.

results.description: One entry per row the undone batch changed, by ID.

items.description: What the undo did to one row.

outcome.description: `created` when the undo put back a row the batch deleted, `replaced` when it put back values the batch changed, `deleted` when it removed a row the batch created, and `unchanged` when the row already stood as it was before the batch.

kind.description: What the archive doesn't hold. `enforcement` appears only when the archive's instance couldn't read its enforcement settings, and `telemetry` only when `secrets_to_set` names a telemetry setting.

message.description: A sentence saying that this kind is not restored and what to do about it.

NotRestored.description: One kind of thing the archive doesn't hold, with what to do about it.

instance_id.description: The ID of the instance that wrote the archive.

destination.description: Where this instance takes its backups: `folder` for a backup folder, `bucket` for an object store, or `null` when it has no backup destination.

kept_by_previous_instance.description: Its `backups/<id>`, `backup-parts/<id>` and `files/<id>` folders in a backup folder, or only `<prefix>/backups/<id>` and `<prefix>/backup-parts/<id>` in a bucket. Empty with none. Delete only once that instance no longer runs.

message.description: A sentence naming that instance and what it keeps, and saying to delete it only once that instance no longer runs and nothing else restores from it.

PreviousInstance.description: The instance that wrote an archive, and what it keeps in this instance's backup destination. Present when the archive was written by another instance than this one.

InvalidClientError.description: An OAuth error in the shape RFC 6749 defines, for a client Marfa does not accept.

error_description.description: A description of the error for a person to read.

tags.description: The item's tags.

ClockConfirmation.description: The time Marfa now trusts, after you confirmed its clock.

confirmed_at.description: The clock's time when you confirmed it, in UTC, now the trusted time.

PasskeyAddLink.description: The page where the owner signs in to add a passkey.

url.description: The sign-in page at the instance's own address, which goes on to the owner's passkey page once the owner signs in. It carries no credential.

AttentionEventFrame.description: A new entry in what needs the owner's attention, sent once when a check first finds it or Marfa first meets a fault. You receive it only with `instance.read`, and only on a stream that names no `type` and isn't a copy stream.

event_type.description: The event, which is also the frame's `event:`.

allOf.description: The new entry: its kind and reference, with a sentence fixed for its kind.

AttentionEventEntry.description: Which entry is new, with a sentence fixed for its kind. The entry's title and description, which can name a file path or an error, are read from `GET /attention`.

kind.description: The entry's `kind`, as `GET /attention` lists it.

description.description: A sentence fixed for the kind, the same for every entry of it.

WebhookAttentionEvent.description: The body of a webhook delivery of a new attention entry.

event_id.description: The event's ID in the log, the same as its `id:` on `GET /events`. Absent from a delivery of a fault sent while the database fails, which no log holds, no delivery list shows and nothing can redeliver.

delivery_id.description: The ID of the delivery, the same on every attempt. Use it to recognize a repeat.

delivered_at.description: When Marfa sent this attempt, in UTC.

published_at.description: When the release was published, in UTC.

UpdateLatest.description: The newest published release Marfa found.

at.description: When the check failed, in UTC.

message.description: Why the check found no release, in words for a person.
message.example: the host could not be reached

UpdateCheckError.description: Why the latest check for a release failed.

state.description: Where the update is. `idle`: none under way. `fetching`: downloading. `checking`: checking the download. `swapping`: putting the new programs in place. `restarting`: the server is ending to start it. `settling`: the release is up, not yet settled.

release.description: The release being moved to, or `null` when `state` is `idle`.

UpdateProgress.description: The update under way, if any.

outcome.description: How the update ended. `succeeded`: the new release stayed up with both its programs in place. `failed`: Marfa did not change the running release, or could not put the old one back. `rolled_back`: Marfa put the old release back.

release.description: The release the update moved to.

finished_at.description: When the update ended, in UTC.

reason.description: Why the update did not succeed, in words for a person, or `null` when it did.

check_enabled.description: `true` if Marfa checks for new releases. See the stored setting `update_check_enabled`.

checked_at.description: When a check last found the newest release, in UTC, or `null` if none has.

check_error.description: Why the latest check failed, or `null` if it did not. A failed check keeps `latest` as it was.

latest.description: The newest published release Marfa found, or `null` if it has found none or the check is off.

method.description: How this server moves to a newer release. `server`: it can update itself when you start an update. `manual`: someone takes the step in `step` on its host.

step.description: What to do on the host to move to `latest`, in plain words, when `available` is `true` and `method` is `manual`; otherwise `null`.

allOf.description: The update under way, if any.

last.description: How the latest update ended, or `null` if none has.

Update.description: Which release this server runs, the newest one Marfa found, and how this server moves to it.
