CloudLinkStart.description: What a link does with the sign-in address.

sign_in_address.description: `move` makes the Marfa Cloud address the sign-in address once linked, which signs everyone out. `keep` leaves the sign-in address as it is.

confirm_sign_in_address_change.description: `true` to confirm the move of the sign-in address. Without it, a move by a recent sign-in on an instance with an owner is refused.

CloudLink.description: This instance's link to Marfa Cloud, which gives it a public name and address.

state.description: `not_linked`: no link, or Marfa Cloud ended it, as `ended` says. `linking`: waiting for approval on Marfa Cloud. `linked`: approved, with a name and address. `failed`: the link ended without linking, as `failure` says.

service_told.description: `false` while Marfa Cloud hasn't been told of an unlink, which Marfa keeps trying to tell it. Present only then, while `state` is `not_linked`.

ended.description: Why the last link ended without an unlink here. Present while `state` is `not_linked` after Marfa Cloud ended the link.

reason.description: `unlinked_by_service`: the link was ended on Marfa Cloud. Marfa put back the sign-in address if the link had moved it, unless `sign_in_address` says it could not.

ended_at.description: When Marfa found the link ended, in UTC.

linking.description: How to approve the link. Present while `state` is `linking`.

user_code.description: The code to enter on Marfa Cloud to approve the link.

approval_url.description: Where to approve the link on Marfa Cloud.

expires_at.description: When the link stops waiting for approval, in UTC, timed on this instance's clock from when it started the link.

port_taken.description: `true` while another program holds the link's port on 127.0.0.1, where Marfa Cloud's connector reaches this instance. Present only then. Free the port, or unlink and link again for another.

name.description: The name Marfa Cloud gave this instance. Present while `state` is `linked`.

address.description: The address Marfa Cloud gave this instance. Present while `state` is `linked`.

linked_at.description: When Marfa Cloud linked this instance, in UTC. Present while `state` is `linked`.

connector.description: The connector that carries traffic through Marfa Cloud. Present while `state` is `linked`.

state.description: The connector's state: `stopped`, `starting`, `connected` (ready and carrying traffic), `reconnecting` (ended or no longer ready, being brought back) or `failed` (can't run; see `reason`).

reason.description: Why a `failed` connector can't run: `missing` (no connector file), `origin_unknown` (the link keeps no port for it; link again), `port_taken` (another program holds its port), `refused` (Marfa Cloud refuses its token) or `token` (no token file).

since.description: Since when the connector has been in this state, in UTC.

sign_in_address.description: Where the sign-in address stands. Present while `state` is `linking` or `linked`, while failed if the sign-in address is the Marfa Cloud address, and while not linked if the link ended with the sign-in address still at its Marfa Cloud address.

state.description: `moved`: it is the Marfa Cloud address. `kept`: it stays as it is. `pending`: Marfa moves it once linked. `waiting`: it moves when you take `next_step`. `not_put_back`: the link ended, and Marfa couldn't move it back from the Marfa Cloud address.

failure.description: Why Marfa couldn't move the sign-in address back. Present while `state` is `not_put_back`, after Marfa Cloud ended the link.

reason.description: The error code of the write that failed.

next_step.description: How to move the sign-in address yourself. Present while linked and `state` is `waiting`, and while `state` is `not_put_back` and `addresses` reads.

request.description: The request that moves it, sent from an app someone signed in to recently.

sign_in_address.description: The address it moves to: the Marfa Cloud address, or for `not_put_back`, the one Marfa would have moved it back to.

confirm_sign_in_address_change.description: Always `true`: the move signs everyone out.

command.description: The `marfa` command that moves it, run where the server runs.

failure.description: Why the link failed. Present while `state` is `failed`.

reason.description: `denied`: the approval was declined. `expired`: it wasn't approved in time. `refused`: Marfa Cloud refused it, as `message` says. `unlinked`: Marfa Cloud ended it. `unreadable`: a secret of the link no longer opens.

message.description: Marfa Cloud's reason for a refusal. Present when `reason` is `refused`.

service_told.description: `true` if Marfa Cloud was told, or took the cancel of a link that was linking. `false` if it couldn't be reached, and Marfa keeps trying. Present when a link was linking or linked.

CloudLinkEventFrame.description: A change to the link to Marfa Cloud. You receive it only with `config.manage`, and only on a stream that names no `type` and isn't a copy stream.

event_type.description: The event, which is also the frame's `event:`.

allOf.description: The link as `GET /cloud/link` returns it.

X-Marfa-Contract.description: The contract version this server speaks, the same integer as the document's `info.version` and the root's `contract`. Sent on every response the application gives, refusals included, so a client can check the answer it is about to read. A client generated for another number cannot trust the body. A request refused by the HTTP layer before it reaches the application, such as one with a malformed host, is answered without it.

X-Marfa-Reach.description: The matching opaque reach, supplied only after a conditional copy read and its snapshot have completed. Successful conditional reads and snapshot-attributed resource refusals carry it with Cache-Control: no-store. Ordinary reads and write receipts carry none.

X-Request-ID.description: This request's identifier, the same one written to the server's request log. Echoes the caller's own `X-Request-ID` when it sends one matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}`, and is a generated UUIDv7 otherwise, so a client can either adopt the server's id or impose its own. Quote it when reporting a problem: it is the one value that finds the request again.

X-Error-Code.description: The machine-readable error code, identical to `error.code` in the body and drawn from the same enum the response schema lists. Read it rather than matching on `error.message`, which is prose written for a person and may be reworded. Present on every error the server renders, including one served from an idempotency record.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying, sent with a rate limit's refusal and with a write turned away while a restore runs. For a rate limit it is rounded up from the time left until the latest end among the limits that are spent, and never fewer than 1, so a client that honors it needs no backoff of its own. While a restore runs it is always 5.

Idempotency-Replayed.description: Sent as `true` when this response was served from the record of an earlier request carrying the same `Idempotency-Key`, rather than by performing the write. It is only ever sent on a replay and only with that value, so its absence means the write was performed. The status and body are the first attempt's, which is why the header can arrive on an error: a recorded 409 replays as a 409. Read a replayed response exactly as the original would have been read: the header says where the answer came from, not that anything went wrong.

WWW-Authenticate.description: The step-up challenge of RFC 9470, sent with `insufficient_user_authentication`: `Bearer error="insufficient_user_authentication", max_age="900"`, where `max_age` is how many seconds old the owner's sign-in may be.

post.description: Creates an item. If `source_id` matches an existing item under the same source, updates that item instead. A repeated `id`, or an update that leaves the item as it is, returns the stored item with `acknowledged: true` and writes nothing.

type.description: The item's type identifier, such as `core.note`.

properties.description: The item's properties, checked against the type's schema. Strict mode refuses an undeclared property as `invalid_properties` (`details.code` `unknown_property`). A whole number whose digits a 64-bit float doesn't keep is refused: send it as a string.

id.description: A UUIDv7 you choose for the item. Leave it out and Marfa creates one. Sending an ID you already created returns the stored item, marked `acknowledged`.

state.description: The item's first lifecycle state, one the type's lifecycle can reach. Defaults to `active`.

occurred_at.description: When the item occurred, as an ISO 8601 time. Defaults to the creation time.

source.description: The source to key and stamp the item with. Defaults to your credential's own; it can also name one of your key's `sources`. An item's source never changes.

source_id.description: The item's identifier at its source, such as a vendor's record ID. With `source`, it is the item's natural key: creating with a key that exists updates that item.

mode.description: `upsert` (the default) updates the item `source_id` matches. `create_only` writes nothing when an item already holds the `source_id` under the source, or the `id`, in any state, and answers `item_exists` (409) with `details.existing_id`.

version.description: The version you read. Used only when `source_id` matches a live item: the update then applies only if the item is still at this version. Ignored otherwise.

allOf.description: The item's tier. Defaults to your key's `default_tier`, else `library`. If `source_id` matches an existing item, leaving it out keeps that item's tier.

capture_latitude.description: The latitude where the item was captured.

capture_longitude.description: The longitude where the item was captured.

tags.description: Tags to put on the item: at most 100, each up to 128 characters.

edges.description: Edges to create with the item, as edge type to a list of IDs of the items they point to. Each points from the new item. Marfa creates the item and all its edges, or none. properties_mode.description: How `properties` applies. `merge` (the default) lays them over the item's properties. `replace` takes them as the whole set, so a property you leave out is cleared.

retype.description: `true` moves the item to `type`. You need write on both types, and the properties the item ends up with must fit the new type. Naming the item's current type changes nothing.

version.description: The version of the item you read, which this update is based on.

version_match.description: `exact` requires the item to still hold `version`, even if the fields changed do not collide. If omitted, a stale write can merge over changes to other fields.

post.description: Creates or updates up to 5,000 items in one call, matching existing items on `(source, source_id)`. The batch is atomic by default: one failed entry rolls it all back. Returns each entry's outcome.

id.description: A UUIDv7 for the item. Leave it out and Marfa creates one. If no item matches the natural key, an `id` naming an existing item matches that item: under `upsert` only a live item you can read.

type.description: The item's type identifier, such as `core.note`.

properties.description: The item's properties, checked against the type's schema. Strict mode refuses an undeclared property as `invalid_properties` (`details.code` `unknown_property`). A whole number whose digits a 64-bit float doesn't keep is refused: send it as a string.

properties_mode.description: How `properties` applies to an existing item, as in `PATCH /items/{id}`. `merge` (the default) lays them over its properties. `replace` takes them as the whole set. A new item takes them whole either way.

source.description: The source to key and stamp the entry's item with, as in `POST /items`. Defaults to your credential's own; it can also name one of your key's `sources`.

source_id.description: The item's identifier at its source. With `source`, it is the natural key that matches an existing item.

version.description: The version you read, used when the entry matches an existing item: the update then applies only if the item is still at this version.

tags.description: Tags to put on the item: at most 100, each up to 128 characters.

edges.description: Edge types to set, each mapped to the IDs of the items the item should now point to. An edge to an ID you still list stays as it is, with its properties. items.description: The entries to write, at most 5,000. An entry with a key this operation doesn't declare is refused as `validation_error`, and `details.unknown_body_fields` names each key.

mode.description: `upsert` (the default) updates the item an entry matches. `create_only` skips it, reporting `skipped` with reason `duplicate_source`, or `duplicate_id` if it matched by `id`.

atomic.description: Whether one failed entry rolls back the whole batch. Defaults to `true`. With `false`, that entry is `errored` and the rest are written.

enable_fanout.description: Whether each write also calls outbound webhooks. Defaults to `false`. Marfa logs the events either way.

retype.description: `true` moves an item to the entry's `type` when the entry resolves an existing item of another type. You need write on both types. Defaults to `false`.

post.description: Creates an API key and returns it with its plaintext `key`, shown only here. If the body names none of `permissions`, the five permission maps and `sources`, the key gets everything you hold; if it names any, the key holds only what it names.

label.description: A name for the key, to tell it apart from your other keys.

source.description: The key's own source, stamped on the items it writes unless a write names a source it claims. No other key that hasn't been revoked or expired may have it as its own, and it can't change later.

sources.description: Sources the key may also write under, besides its own `source`. Several keys may claim one source, so their writes share natural keys. You can grant your own `source` and your claims, or with `keys.manage` any source; the local command can grant any.

permissions.description: The permissions to give the key, such as `audit.read`.

allOf.description: The tier an item this key creates goes to when the write names none. Leave it out for `library`.

type_permissions.description: Item types the key may `read` or `write`, by type ID or a wildcard such as `core.*` or `*`. `none` denies a type a wildcard covers.

extension_permissions.description: Extension namespaces the key may `read` or `write`, by namespace or `*`.

edge_permissions.description: Edge types the key may `read` or `write`, by edge type, a namespace wildcard such as `user.*`, or `*`.

metadata_permissions.description: Registrations the key may make: `types` to register types and `edge_types` to register edge types, at `write`. `*` covers both.

allOf.description: Profile access by `name`, `username`, `email`, `avatar`, or `*`. `write` implies read. `write` on a field changes it, and only `username` at `write` changes the username. `*` reads every field and at `write` changes every field but the username.
Enforcement levers for this key alone. Leave it out for none, so the key follows the instance's.

expires_at.description: When the key stops working, as an ISO 8601 date and time in the future. Leave it out for a key that never expires, or, if your own key expires, for one that expires when yours does. It can't be later than your own key's `expires_at`.

owner_key.description: `true` if the key is the owner's, not the app's you act for: it carries no `oauth_client_id`, and disconnecting or narrowing that app leaves it working. From an app, or a key an app made, it needs `keys.manage`.

201.description: Returns the new key with its plaintext `key`. When the local command creates an ordinary key from a body naming no permission, map or `sources`, the key holds every permission and `*: write` on every map, and claims no source.

400.description:
- `missing_required_field`: `label` or `source` is missing, or a lever in `enforcement_override` lacks `types` or `sources`.
- `validation_error`: a field is invalid, such as an unknown permission level, more than 1,000 `sources`, an `expires_at` that isn't a future time, an `owner_key` that isn't `true` or `false`, or a `source` or claim starting `oauth:` or `restored:`.

401.description: `unauthorized`: the request has no credential, or its credential is not valid. For a key that has expired, `details.expired_at` says when it expired.

403.description: - `forbidden`: you lack `keys.mint` and aren't the local command; the body names a permission or map entry you don't hold, a claim, or another key's claim as `source`, that you can't grant, an own `source` a connector holds without `keys.manage`, an `expires_at` past your key's, `owner_key` from an app without `keys.manage`, or `enforcement_override` without `config.manage`. `details` names it.

- `conflict`: another key that hasn't been revoked or expired already has this `source` as its own. `details.source` names it. To let two keys write under one source, claim it in `sources` instead.

put.description: Replaces the instance configuration with the body and returns it. A setting you leave out goes back to its default, so send the whole configuration with your change. To change only some settings, use `PATCH`. Requires `config.manage`.

instance_id.description: This instance's ID, accepted so you can send back what `GET /config` returned. It sets nothing.

version_recent_days.description: Days within which every version is kept. Zero makes this window empty. Absent: the environment default applies.

version_daily_snapshot_days.description: Days within which a daily version is kept. Must be at least `version_recent_days`. Absent: the environment default applies.

version_weekly_snapshot_days.description: Days within which a weekly version is kept. Must be at least `version_daily_snapshot_days`. Absent: the environment default applies.

version_max_versions.description: Maximum versions per item, after applying the time windows. Per-type policy overrides these instance defaults.

grant_inactivity_days.description: Disconnect apps unused for this many days. Zero disables retirement.

enrichment_enabled.description: `true` if Marfa reads text and dimensions from files. An active extraction can finish after disabling. Absent: the environment default applies.

enrichment_ocr_enabled.description: `true` if file reading includes image text. Enabling reconsiders previously skipped images. Absent: the environment default applies.

error_reporting_enabled.description: `true` if exception reports are sent. Enabling requires both `posthog_host` and `posthog_project_token`. Absent: the environment default applies.

heartbeat_enabled.description: `true` if scheduled heartbeat requests are sent. Enabling requires `heartbeat_url`. Absent: the environment default applies.

name.description: The instance's display name, without control or bidirectional formatting characters. Spaces at each end are trimmed. Absent: `Marfa`.

allOf.description: Types on which a write may not set a property the type doesn't declare.
Types that take new items only from the listed sources.

Types whose listings, searches, exports, event streams and webhook deliveries show only items from the listed sources. A read by ID isn't narrowed, and a copy stream sends such items with `listed: false`.

enforcement.description: The instance's enforcement levers. Each applies to every credential that doesn't set the same lever itself. Absent: no lever is on.

audit_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps audit log entries and outbound webhook delivery history. `0` keeps them with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

event_log_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps events, which a stream can replay from a cursor, and the answers it replays for an `Idempotency-Key`. `0` keeps them with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

trash_retention_days.description: Days an item stays in the trash before Marfa purges it. `0` keeps them with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

row_log_retention_days.description: Days a table keeps a batch in its change log, so you can undo it. `0` keeps them with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

inbound_handled_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps inbound webhook deliveries a connector has marked handled. `0` keeps them with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

inbound_pending_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps inbound webhook deliveries no connector has marked handled. `0` keeps them with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

addresses.description: The addresses people reach this instance at, each an origin with no path. The sign-in address is always one of them.

sign_in_address.description: The address people sign in at, an origin with no path. Absent: this computer's own address.

confirm_sign_in_address_change.description: `true` to confirm a change that moves the sign-in address of a claimed instance. It sets nothing.

skip_sign_in_address_check.description: `true` moves the sign-in address without first checking that it answers as this instance, for a host that answers only after the move. Only the private local command can send it.

backup_path.description: The absolute path of the folder Marfa backs itself up to and keeps a second copy of each file in, outside the data directory and the blob folder. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: no backup folder.

object_store_bucket.description: The bucket of an S3-compatible object store that also keeps each file and the backups: 1 to 255 ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `:`, `-` and `_`, other than `.` and `..`. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes, and removes `object_store_secret_access_key` unless the same request sets it. Absent: no object store.

object_store_region.description: The region of the object store: a name of 1 to 63 ASCII letters, digits, hyphens and underscores that can be part of a host name, such as `us-east-1` or `auto`. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: `us-east-1`.

object_store_endpoint.description: The endpoint of the object store, an `http` or `https` URL with no user name or password. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes, and removes `object_store_secret_access_key` unless the same request sets it. Absent: the store's provider chooses it.

object_store_path_style.description: `true` if the store at `object_store_endpoint` is addressed by path. `false` puts the bucket, as lowercase host labels, before the endpoint's host, a name without the bucket. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: `true`.

object_store_prefix.description: The folder in the bucket Marfa keeps files and backups under, as `/`-joined segments. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: `marfa`.

object_store_access_key_id.description: The access key ID for the object store.

allow_private_addresses.description: `true` if Marfa may send webhooks, the heartbeat, exception reports and object store requests to loopback, private and other addresses that aren't public. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: `false`.

object_store_secret_access_key.description: The secret access key for the object store, with no whitespace around it. Marfa never returns it. A `PUT` that leaves it out keeps it, unless the `PUT` changes `object_store_bucket` or `object_store_endpoint`; `PATCH` with `null` removes it.

heartbeat_url.description: The `http` or `https` URL Marfa requests on a schedule, so that something else can notice when the requests stop. Marfa never returns it. A `PUT` that leaves it out keeps it; `PATCH` with `null` removes it.

posthog_host.description: The PostHog host Marfa sends a report of each of its own faults to, for PostHog's error tracking. It must be an `https` URL, or an `http` URL on this machine, with no user name or password, and it needs `posthog_project_token` set too. Marfa never returns it. A `PUT` that leaves it out keeps it; `PATCH` with `null` removes it.

posthog_project_token.description: The PostHog project token Marfa sends its fault reports with, with no whitespace around it. It needs `posthog_host` set too. Marfa never returns it. A `PUT` that leaves it out keeps it; `PATCH` with `null` removes it.

telemetry_enabled.description: `true` if Marfa sends telemetry about itself: traces, log records and metrics to the OTLP endpoints, and exception reports to `posthog_host`. `false` sends none of them and keeps every telemetry setting. Absent: `true`.

otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint.description: The base URL of the OTLP receiver Marfa exports traces to, under `v1/traces`, log records to, under `v1/logs`, and metrics to, under `v1/metrics`, keeping its query. Marfa never returns it. A `PUT` that leaves it out keeps it; `PATCH` with `null` removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_traces_endpoint.description: The URL Marfa posts traces to, used as written, in place of the one under `otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint`, which must also be set. Marfa never returns it. A `PUT` that leaves it out keeps it; `PATCH` with `null` removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_logs_endpoint.description: The URL Marfa posts log records to, used as written, in place of the one under `otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint`, which must also be set. Marfa never returns it. A `PUT` that leaves it out keeps it; `PATCH` with `null` removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_metrics_endpoint.description: The URL Marfa posts metrics to, used as written, in place of the one under `otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint`, which must also be set. Marfa never returns it. A `PUT` that leaves it out keeps it; `PATCH` with `null` removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_headers.description: The headers Marfa sends with every OTLP export, as comma-separated `key=value` pairs with percent-encoded values and no whitespace around them. Marfa never returns it. A `PUT` that leaves it out keeps it; `PATCH` with `null` removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_traces_headers.description: The headers Marfa sends with trace exports, as comma-separated `key=value` pairs with percent-encoded values. One here replaces the one of the same name in `otel_exporter_otlp_headers`. Marfa never returns it. A `PUT` that leaves it out keeps it; `PATCH` with `null` removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_logs_headers.description: The headers Marfa sends with log exports, as comma-separated `key=value` pairs with percent-encoded values. One here replaces the one of the same name in `otel_exporter_otlp_headers`. Marfa never returns it. A `PUT` that leaves it out keeps it; `PATCH` with `null` removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_metrics_headers.description: The headers Marfa sends with metric exports, as comma-separated `key=value` pairs with percent-encoded values. One here replaces the one of the same name in `otel_exporter_otlp_headers`. Marfa never returns it. A `PUT` that leaves it out keeps it; `PATCH` with `null` removes it.

otel_sample_ratio.description: The share of traces Marfa exports, from 0 to 1. A trace that holds an error is exported whatever this says. Absent: `0.05`.

otel_service_name.description: The service name on everything Marfa exports, in place of a `service.name` in `otel_resource_attributes`. Absent: `marfa-server`. An archive doesn't carry it.

otel_resource_attributes.description: Attributes Marfa adds to everything it exports, as comma-separated `key=value` pairs with percent-encoded values. One named here replaces Marfa's own of the same name, such as `service.version`. An archive doesn't carry it.

secrets_set.description: The secret settings `GET /config` says are set, accepted so you can send back what it returned. It sets nothing.

max_request_bytes.description: The largest request body Marfa accepts, in bytes. Marfa waits 180 seconds for a body, so a body over about 21 MiB can't arrive in time over a 1 Mbit/s link. Absent: the server's default applies.

max_bulk_request_bytes.description: The largest body the bulk operations accept, in bytes, and the largest row a restore reads. The most you can set is 33554432, half the 67108864 bytes a restore reads on one archive line. Absent: the server's default applies.

disk_reserve_bytes.description: Free disk space an upload must leave on the blob volume, in bytes. `0` refuses no write for room, and health still reports the disk as degraded below 64 MiB. Absent: the server's default applies.

blob_min_copies.description: The fewest live copies Marfa keeps of each blob. Absent: the server's default applies.

blob_cleanup_enabled.description: `true` if the `blob-orphans` job purges blobs nothing references once they have stood in the orphan report for `blob_cleanup_grace_seconds`. Absent: the server's default applies.

blob_cleanup_grace_seconds.description: How long a blob nothing references stands in the orphan report before a later run purges it, in seconds. Absent: the server's default applies.

backup_interval_seconds.description: How often Marfa makes a backup when anything it holds has changed, in seconds. `0` turns scheduled backups off. Absent: the server's default applies.

rate_limit_enabled.description: `true` if the rate limiter is on for requests a key or app makes, app registrations, device code requests, passkey sign-in challenges and deliveries to inbound addresses. Absent: the server's default applies.

rate_limit_requests.description: How many requests one key or app may make in each rate-limit window, across every operation. Absent: the server's default applies.

rate_limit_keys_requests.description: How many requests one key may make in each rate-limit window to the operations under `/keys`. Absent: the server's default applies.

rate_limit_window_seconds.description: How long one rate-limit window lasts, in seconds. Absent: the server's default applies.

unapproved_app_retention_hours.description: Hours Marfa keeps an app that registered itself and holds no grant. `0` keeps it with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

revoked_grant_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps a revoked app grant. `0` keeps it with no age limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

enrichment_max_blob_bytes.description: The largest file Marfa reads whole to extract its text, in bytes. Marfa skips a larger file unread, and reads a sound or video from its headers whatever its size. Absent: the server's default applies.

enrichment_max_text_chars.description: The most Unicode characters of extracted text Marfa keeps, counted as characters and not UTF-16 code units. Marfa cuts longer text short. Absent: the server's default applies.

enrichment_max_inflated_bytes.description: The most a document may inflate to when Marfa extracts its text, all its parts together, in bytes. Marfa skips a document that inflates past it. Absent: the server's default applies.

enrichment_max_memory_bytes.description: The most memory the process that reads one file may take, in bytes. Marfa skips a file that needs more. Absent: the server's default applies.

enrichment_max_attempts.description: How many times Marfa tries to read a file that fails, or that stops the server, before it stops trying. Absent: the server's default applies.

update_check_enabled.description: `true` if Marfa checks GitHub for new releases every few hours. When `false`, it makes no request for them and reports no release as newer. Absent: the server's default applies.

event_stream_max_viewers.description: The most event-stream viewers one server serves at once. `0` sets no limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

mcp_fetch_enabled.description: `true` if MCP tools fetch a file from a web address, or a file a chat attached, to save it. When `false`, a tool asked to fetch one is refused. Absent: the server's default applies.

mcp_fetch_max_bytes.description: The largest file an MCP tool fetches from a web address to save, in bytes. Marfa refuses a larger file and stores nothing. Absent: the server's default applies.

mcp_fetch_timeout_seconds.description: How long an MCP tool's fetch of a file from a web address may take, from connecting to the last byte, in seconds. Absent: the server's default applies.

inbound_max_bytes.description: The largest inbound webhook delivery Marfa stores, in bytes. Absent: the server's default applies.

rate_limit_inbound_requests.description: How many requests one inbound endpoint's address takes in each rate-limit window, whatever each is answered. Absent: the server's default applies.

inbound_in_flight_bytes.description: The most bytes of inbound webhook deliveries Marfa holds in memory at once. One source holds at most half. Absent: the server's default applies.

inbound_backlog_deliveries.description: The unhandled deliveries one registration may hold before Marfa refuses more for it. Absent: the server's default applies.

inbound_backlog_bytes.description: The bytes of unhandled deliveries one registration may hold before Marfa refuses more for it. Absent: the server's default applies.

webhook_backlog_deliveries.description: Maximum number of pending deliveries per webhook. Marfa records a new delivery as `canceled` if adding it would exceed this limit. Absent: the server's default applies.

webhook_backlog_bytes.description: Maximum total payload size in bytes for a webhook's pending deliveries. Marfa records a new delivery as `canceled` if adding its payload would exceed this total. Absent: the server's default applies.

inbound_retained_deliveries.description: The most deliveries one registration retains across its live and retired endpoints. Absent: the server's default applies.

inbound_retained_bytes.description: The most bytes of bodies, headers and queries one registration retains across its live and retired endpoints. Absent: the server's default applies.

cors_origins.description: The browser origins allowed to call the API across origins with a token, beside the web pages the owner approves. Each is an origin with no path. Absent: the server's default applies.

200.description: Returns the configuration as stored, with `sign_in_moved` when the write moved the sign-in address.

400.description:
- `missing_required_field`: a lever lacks `types` or `sources`.
- `validation_error`: the body names a setting Marfa doesn't know, a value is out of range, the effective version windows are out of order, reporting is turned from off to on without a configured receiver, the name is invalid, or `instance_id` names a different instance.

401.description:
- `unauthorized`: the request has no credential, or its credential is not valid. For a key that has expired, `details.expired_at` says when it expired.
- `insufficient_user_authentication`: your app's owner signed in more than fifteen minutes ago. Send them through `GET /oauth/authorize` with `max_age`.

403.description:
- `forbidden`: you don't hold `config.manage`, which `details.required_scope` names, or the body sets `skip_sign_in_address_check`, which only the private local command can send.
- `app_sign_in_required`: the change needs a recent sign-in, and you are an API key. A person makes it from an app they signed in to, or with the private local command.

408.description: `request_timeout`: the request body didn't arrive whole within 180 seconds. Nothing changed, and Marfa closed the connection. Send the request again. A body larger than about 21 MiB can't arrive in that time over a 1 Mbit/s link, so send it in smaller requests.

409.description:

- `instance_changed`: `X-Marfa-Instance-Id` names another instance.
- `sign_in_address_change_unconfirmed`: the body lacks `confirm_sign_in_address_change: true`. `details.consequences` lists the effects.
- `sign_in_address_check_failed`: the new sign-in address did not answer as this instance. `details.reason` says why.

412.description: `contract_mismatch`: `X-Marfa-Contract` names another contract version than this instance speaks, or is not a whole number. Nothing was done.

413.description: `request_too_large`: the request body is larger than this instance accepts.

429.description: `rate_limited`: you sent too many requests. Wait for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`, then try again.

500.description: `internal_error`: Marfa failed in a way it didn't expect, and the request may not have completed. Read what you changed before you repeat a write.

503.description: `write_contention`: the database was busy, and Marfa couldn't complete the request in time. Nothing changed. Try the request again. While a restore runs, `details.reason` is `restore_running`.

507.description: `insufficient_storage`: the disk that holds the instance's data has no room for the request, or the request would leave less free than the instance keeps in reserve. Nothing changed, unless `details.write_outcome` is `unknown`, which means the write may have landed: read what you changed before you repeat it. Free space on the disk, then try the request again.

parameters.name: X-Marfa-Instance-Id
parameters.description: The ID of the instance you expect, as `GET /` returns it. If another instance answers at this address, Marfa returns `409 instance_changed` and doesn't write. Leave it out to send the request to whichever instance answers.

patch.description: Updates the named settings and returns the configuration. Unnamed settings stay, except the store secret when its bucket or endpoint changes; `null` removes a setting. Send all `enforcement` levers you want on; requires `config.manage`.

version_recent_days.description: Days within which every version is kept. Zero makes this window empty. Absent: the environment default applies. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

version_daily_snapshot_days.description: Days within which a daily version is kept. Must be at least `version_recent_days`. Absent: the environment default applies. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

version_weekly_snapshot_days.description: Days within which a weekly version is kept. Must be at least `version_daily_snapshot_days`. Absent: the environment default applies. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

version_max_versions.description: Maximum versions per item, after applying the time windows. Per-type policy overrides these instance defaults. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

grant_inactivity_days.description: Disconnect apps unused for this many days. Zero disables retirement. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

enrichment_enabled.description: `true` if Marfa reads text and dimensions from files. An active extraction can finish after disabling. Absent: the environment default applies. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

enrichment_ocr_enabled.description: `true` if file reading includes image text. Enabling reconsiders previously skipped images. Absent: the environment default applies. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

error_reporting_enabled.description: `true` if exception reports are sent. Enabling requires both `posthog_host` and `posthog_project_token`. Absent: the environment default applies. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

heartbeat_enabled.description: `true` if scheduled heartbeat requests are sent. Enabling requires `heartbeat_url`. Absent: the environment default applies. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

instance_id.description: This instance's ID, accepted so you can send back what `GET /config` returned. It sets nothing.

name.description: The instance's display name. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

allOf.description: Types on which a write may not set a property the type doesn't declare.
Types that take new items only from the listed sources.

Types whose listings, searches, exports, event streams and webhook deliveries show only items from the listed sources. A read by ID isn't narrowed, and a copy stream sends such items with `listed: false`.

enforcement.description: The instance's enforcement levers. Sending this replaces all three levers, so include every lever you want on. `null` removes them all.

audit_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps audit log entries and outbound webhook delivery history. `0` keeps them with no age limit. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

event_log_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps events, which a stream can replay from a cursor, and the answers it replays for an `Idempotency-Key`. `0` keeps them with no age limit. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

trash_retention_days.description: Days an item stays in the trash before Marfa purges it. `0` keeps them with no age limit. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

row_log_retention_days.description: Days a table keeps a batch in its change log, so you can undo it. `0` keeps them with no age limit. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

inbound_handled_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps inbound webhook deliveries a connector has marked handled. `0` keeps them with no age limit. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

inbound_pending_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps inbound webhook deliveries no connector has marked handled. `0` keeps them with no age limit. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

addresses.description: The addresses people reach this instance at, each an origin with no path. The sign-in address is always one of them. `null` removes them, so the server's default applies.

sign_in_address.description: The address people sign in at, an origin with no path. Absent: this computer's own address. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

confirm_sign_in_address_change.description: `true` to confirm a change that moves the sign-in address of a claimed instance. It sets nothing.

skip_sign_in_address_check.description: `true` moves the sign-in address without first checking that it answers as this instance, for a host that answers only after the move. Only the private local command can send it.

backup_path.description: The absolute path of the folder Marfa backs itself up to and keeps a second copy of each file in, outside the data directory and the blob folder. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: no backup folder. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

object_store_bucket.description: The bucket of an S3-compatible object store that also keeps each file and the backups: 1 to 255 ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `:`, `-` and `_`, other than `.` and `..`. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes, and removes `object_store_secret_access_key` unless the same request sets it. Absent: no object store. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

object_store_region.description: The region of the object store: a name of 1 to 63 ASCII letters, digits, hyphens and underscores that can be part of a host name, such as `us-east-1` or `auto`. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: `us-east-1`. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

object_store_endpoint.description: The endpoint of the object store, an `http` or `https` URL with no user name or password. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes, and removes `object_store_secret_access_key` unless the same request sets it. Absent: the store's provider chooses it. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

object_store_path_style.description: `true` if the store at `object_store_endpoint` is addressed by path. `false` puts the bucket, as lowercase host labels, before the endpoint's host, a name without the bucket. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: `true`. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

object_store_prefix.description: The folder in the bucket Marfa keeps files and backups under, as `/`-joined segments. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: `marfa`. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

object_store_access_key_id.description: The access key ID for the object store. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

allow_private_addresses.description: `true` if Marfa may send webhooks, the heartbeat, exception reports and object store requests to loopback, private and other addresses that aren't public. Changing it needs a sign-in from the last fifteen minutes. Absent: `false`. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

object_store_secret_access_key.description: The secret access key for the object store, with no whitespace around it. Marfa never returns it. `null` or an empty string removes it, and so does a change to `object_store_bucket` or `object_store_endpoint` that doesn't set it.

heartbeat_url.description: The `http` or `https` URL Marfa requests on a schedule, so that something else can notice when the requests stop. Marfa never returns it. `null` or an empty string removes it.

posthog_host.description: The PostHog host Marfa sends a report of each of its own faults to, for PostHog's error tracking. It must be an `https` URL, or an `http` URL on this machine, with no user name or password, and it needs `posthog_project_token` set too. Marfa never returns it. `null` or an empty string removes it.

posthog_project_token.description: The PostHog project token Marfa sends its fault reports with, with no whitespace around it. It needs `posthog_host` set too. Marfa never returns it. `null` or an empty string removes it.

telemetry_enabled.description: `true` if Marfa sends telemetry about itself: traces, log records and metrics to the OTLP endpoints, and exception reports to `posthog_host`. `false` sends none of them and keeps every telemetry setting. Absent: `true`. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint.description: The base URL of the OTLP receiver Marfa exports traces to, under `v1/traces`, log records to, under `v1/logs`, and metrics to, under `v1/metrics`, keeping its query. Marfa never returns it. `null` or an empty string removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_traces_endpoint.description: The URL Marfa posts traces to, used as written, in place of the one under `otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint`, which must also be set. Marfa never returns it. `null` or an empty string removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_logs_endpoint.description: The URL Marfa posts log records to, used as written, in place of the one under `otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint`, which must also be set. Marfa never returns it. `null` or an empty string removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_metrics_endpoint.description: The URL Marfa posts metrics to, used as written, in place of the one under `otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint`, which must also be set. Marfa never returns it. `null` or an empty string removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_headers.description: The headers Marfa sends with every OTLP export, as comma-separated `key=value` pairs with percent-encoded values and no whitespace around them. Marfa never returns it. `null` or an empty string removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_traces_headers.description: The headers Marfa sends with trace exports, as comma-separated `key=value` pairs with percent-encoded values. One here replaces the one of the same name in `otel_exporter_otlp_headers`. Marfa never returns it. `null` or an empty string removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_logs_headers.description: The headers Marfa sends with log exports, as comma-separated `key=value` pairs with percent-encoded values. One here replaces the one of the same name in `otel_exporter_otlp_headers`. Marfa never returns it. `null` or an empty string removes it.

otel_exporter_otlp_metrics_headers.description: The headers Marfa sends with metric exports, as comma-separated `key=value` pairs with percent-encoded values. One here replaces the one of the same name in `otel_exporter_otlp_headers`. Marfa never returns it. `null` or an empty string removes it.

otel_sample_ratio.description: The share of traces Marfa exports, from 0 to 1. A trace that holds an error is exported whatever this says. Absent: `0.05`. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

otel_service_name.description: The service name on everything Marfa exports, in place of a `service.name` in `otel_resource_attributes`. Absent: `marfa-server`. An archive doesn't carry it. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

otel_resource_attributes.description: Attributes Marfa adds to everything it exports, as comma-separated `key=value` pairs with percent-encoded values. One named here replaces Marfa's own of the same name, such as `service.version`. An archive doesn't carry it. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

secrets_set.description: The secret settings `GET /config` says are set, accepted so you can send back what it returned. It sets nothing.

max_request_bytes.description: The largest request body Marfa accepts, in bytes. Marfa waits 180 seconds for a body, so a body over about 21 MiB can't arrive in time over a 1 Mbit/s link. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

max_bulk_request_bytes.description: The largest body the bulk operations accept, in bytes, and the largest row a restore reads. The most you can set is 33554432, half the 67108864 bytes a restore reads on one archive line. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

disk_reserve_bytes.description: Free disk space an upload must leave on the blob volume, in bytes. `0` refuses no write for room, and health still reports the disk as degraded below 64 MiB. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

blob_min_copies.description: The fewest live copies Marfa keeps of each blob. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

blob_cleanup_enabled.description: `true` if the `blob-orphans` job purges blobs nothing references once they have stood in the orphan report for `blob_cleanup_grace_seconds`. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

blob_cleanup_grace_seconds.description: How long a blob nothing references stands in the orphan report before a later run purges it, in seconds. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

backup_interval_seconds.description: How often Marfa makes a backup when anything it holds has changed, in seconds. `0` turns scheduled backups off. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

rate_limit_enabled.description: `true` if the rate limiter is on for requests a key or app makes, app registrations, device code requests, passkey sign-in challenges and deliveries to inbound addresses. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

rate_limit_requests.description: How many requests one key or app may make in each rate-limit window, across every operation. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

rate_limit_keys_requests.description: How many requests one key may make in each rate-limit window to the operations under `/keys`. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

rate_limit_window_seconds.description: How long one rate-limit window lasts, in seconds. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

unapproved_app_retention_hours.description: Hours Marfa keeps an app that registered itself and holds no grant. `0` keeps it with no age limit. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

revoked_grant_retention_days.description: Days Marfa keeps a revoked app grant. `0` keeps it with no age limit. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

enrichment_max_blob_bytes.description: The largest file Marfa reads whole to extract its text, in bytes. Marfa skips a larger file unread, and reads a sound or video from its headers whatever its size. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

enrichment_max_text_chars.description: The most Unicode characters of extracted text Marfa keeps, counted as characters and not UTF-16 code units. Marfa cuts longer text short. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

enrichment_max_inflated_bytes.description: The most a document may inflate to when Marfa extracts its text, all its parts together, in bytes. Marfa skips a document that inflates past it. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

enrichment_max_memory_bytes.description: The most memory the process that reads one file may take, in bytes. Marfa skips a file that needs more. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

enrichment_max_attempts.description: How many times Marfa tries to read a file that fails, or that stops the server, before it stops trying. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

update_check_enabled.description: `true` if Marfa checks GitHub for new releases every few hours. When `false`, it makes no request for them and reports no release as newer. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

event_stream_max_viewers.description: The most event-stream viewers one server serves at once. `0` sets no limit. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

mcp_fetch_enabled.description: `true` if MCP tools fetch a file from a web address, or a file a chat attached, to save it. When `false`, a tool asked to fetch one is refused. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

mcp_fetch_max_bytes.description: The largest file an MCP tool fetches from a web address to save, in bytes. Marfa refuses a larger file and stores nothing. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

mcp_fetch_timeout_seconds.description: How long an MCP tool's fetch of a file from a web address may take, from connecting to the last byte, in seconds. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

inbound_max_bytes.description: The largest inbound webhook delivery Marfa stores, in bytes. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

rate_limit_inbound_requests.description: How many requests one inbound endpoint's address takes in each rate-limit window, whatever each is answered. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

inbound_in_flight_bytes.description: The most bytes of inbound webhook deliveries Marfa holds in memory at once. One source holds at most half. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

inbound_backlog_deliveries.description: The unhandled deliveries one registration may hold before Marfa refuses more for it. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

inbound_backlog_bytes.description: The bytes of unhandled deliveries one registration may hold before Marfa refuses more for it. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

webhook_backlog_deliveries.description: Maximum number of pending deliveries per webhook. Marfa records a new delivery as `canceled` if adding it would exceed this limit. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

webhook_backlog_bytes.description: Maximum total payload size in bytes for a webhook's pending deliveries. Marfa records a new delivery as `canceled` if adding its payload would exceed this total. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

inbound_retained_deliveries.description: The most deliveries one registration retains across its live and retired endpoints. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

inbound_retained_bytes.description: The most bytes of bodies, headers and queries one registration retains across its live and retired endpoints. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

cors_origins.description: The browser origins allowed to call the API across origins with a token, beside the web pages the owner approves. Each is an origin with no path. `null` removes it, so the server's default applies.

200.description: Returns the counts. Items and edges keep their IDs, versions, dates and history, even if their type now refuses them or is gone. An item whose ID, natural key or link is taken is left as it is, and a setting, icon, source name or connector state is set only where none is. An archive holds no sign-in, keys, apps, webhooks or tombstones.

duplicates.description: How many items Marfa skipped because their ID, natural key or link is already taken.

edges_skipped_reasons.description: How many edges Marfa skipped for each reason, such as `endpoint_missing` or `already_present`.

blobs_imported.description: How many blobs the archive carried whose bytes match their hash, whether or not the instance already had them.

entries_skipped.description: The name of each archive entry Marfa doesn't know and skipped, such as one a tar tool adds, in the order the archive holds them.

400.description:

401.description:
- `unauthorized`: the request has no credential, or its credential is not valid. For a key that has expired, `details.expired_at` says when it expired.

403.description:

408.description: - `request_timeout`: no bytes of the archive arrived for 60 seconds. Nothing was written. An upload has no other time limit while bytes keep arriving.

409.description:
- `conflict`: the archive redefines a type this instance registers differently or registered while the restore ran, carries a core edge type, or carries a snapshot ID that already exists.

413.description: - `request_too_large`: an item's properties, the properties of one of its earlier versions, or an edge's properties are larger than the bulk write endpoints accept. `details` names the line and the field.

500.description: `internal_error`: Marfa failed in a way it didn't expect, and the request may not have completed. Read what you changed before you repeat a write.

503.description:
- `blob_store_unavailable`: a blob store failed, or didn't answer in time, while Marfa checked a blob's copy, or a store hasn't finished an earlier write or delete of a blob the archive names. Nothing was written. Try again later.
- `write_contention`: the database was busy, and Marfa couldn't complete the request in time. Nothing changed. Try the request again.

507.description: `insufficient_storage`: the disk that holds the instance's data has no room for the request, or the request would leave less free than the instance keeps in reserve. post.description: Marfa sends this request to a webhook's `url` for each event it subscribes to, with only what the webhook's credential can read when it's sent. A delivery can arrive more than once: use `delivery_id` to recognize a repeat.

parameters.name: X-Marfa-Signature
parameters.description: `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, where `v1` is the HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<raw body>` under the webhook's `secret`. Check it, and that `t` is recent, before you trust the body.

parameters.name: X-Marfa-Event-Type
parameters.description: The event, the same as `event_type` in the body.

2XX.description: Marfa records the delivery as `succeeded`. It doesn't read the response body.

default.description: Any other answer is a failure. On a `3xx`, or a `4xx` other than `408` and `429`, the delivery becomes `failed`. On a `408`, `429` or `5xx`, no answer within 10 seconds or no connection, Marfa tries again after at least 1, 5, 25, 125, 625, 3125 and 15625 seconds, and as long as `Retry-After` asks, up to 5 minutes. After 8 attempts, it's `failed`.

tags.name: Items

tags.description: JSON objects attached to an item, one per namespace.

tags.description: Typed, directed relationships between items.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Full-text search across items.

tags.name: Types

tags.name: Edge types
tags.description: The types edges can have, each with its cardinality and cascade rule.

tags.name: Blobs
tags.description: Bytes stored by content hash, and the stores that hold them.

tags.name: Event stream
tags.description: Changes to items, table rows and edges, streamed as they happen.

tags.description: Changes sent to a URL you choose, and each delivery's record. Keys and apps use these endpoints; the owner's browser session can't.

tags.name: Folders

tags.name: Views
